The four-dimension breakdown and the 95% PASS thresholds are the series' own decomposition, but the text attributes them to the KSI itself as if the indicator enumerates four dimensions. No in-repo source supports that attribution; a reviewer tracing the KSI text would not find four dimensions or a 95% threshold in it.
findings.fix: Attribute the model to the series: 'the four training dimensions this program decomposes KSI-CED-RAT review into' and 'the substrate's PASS thresholds', not 'the KSI evaluates/requires'.

findings.claim: The JSON schema example (lines 473-522: review_period, generated_date, dimensions.*, completion_rate) vs the figure directly below it (line 524 fig-alt: required fields overall_completion_pct, snapshot_date, cp3_tabletop_date, ir2_drill_date, role_tiers[] with tier_completion_pct)
findings.problem: Two different field sets are both presented as THE training-effectiveness-record schema — the record that is the KSI-022 evidence contract. The deck spec (slide 11) uses the figure's field names, not the JSON example's. Since the whole claim is that the substrate queries this machine-readable record, an assessor would reject the contract as ambiguous: which field does slot_binding actually read — completion_rate or overall_completion_pct? Note AAN_Evidence_Contract_Spec.md defines slot-08 (training) but does not carry this signal's field schema, so nothing in-repo arbitrates.
findings.fix: Pick one canonical field set, make the JSON example and the figure/deck agree, and register the schema (or a pointer to its UIAO-side definition) so the contract has one shape.

findings.claim: "The annual tabletop exercise directly tests the CP-2 Contingency Plan" (line 414) and 'Annual tabletop exercise with attendance record' (line 130) vs the CP-3 calendar of FOUR quarterly exercises (lines 417-424) and PASS criterion 'tabletop run' singular (line 642)
findings.problem: CP-3 evidence cadence is stated inconsistently: one annual tabletop in the closure table and PASS criteria, four quarterly exercises in the calendar, and the schema example shows 1 tabletop in a single quarter. A reviewer cannot determine what evidence volume satisfies CP-3 (1/year or 4/year). Additionally, the Q1/Q2/Q4 entries are functional failover TESTS, which map to CP-4 (Contingency Plan Testing) at least as much as to CP-3 training — expect a mapping challenge.
findings.fix: State one cadence (e.g., 'four quarterly exercises, of which Q3 is the full CP-3 tabletop; Q1/Q2/Q4 are functional tests supporting CP-4') and align lines 130, 414, 592, and 642.

findings.claim: "the 72-hour reporting window" for a PII breach (Tier 5 data-steward training content)
findings.problem: No in-repo SSOT supports a 72-hour federal PII-breach window, and it conflicts with the widely applicable federal requirement (OMB M-17-12: report suspected/confirmed PII breaches to US-CERT/CISA within one hour); 72 hours is the GDPR figure. If this is an SSA-internal policy window it needs a citation; as written a hostile ISSO would challenge it as importing the wrong regime into federal training content.
findings.fix: Cite the actual authority (OMB M-17-12 one-hour US-CERT report plus any SSA breach-response policy timeline) or remove the number.

findings.claim: Graph API integration requires permission 'LearningAssignmentReport.Read.All' against endpoint v1.0/employeeExperience/learningCourseActivities (lines 536-546; repeated in the Phase 1 checklist at line 698 and deck spec slide 13)
findings.problem: The permission name and endpoint pairing is load-bearing for the AT-4 pipeline (Phase 1 checklist item) but is not verifiable in-repo, and the documented Graph permissions for learningCourseActivities are the LearningAssignedCourse/LearningSelfInitiatedCourse family — 'LearningAssignmentReport.Read.All' may not exist as named. Cannot judge true/false here; must be verified against Microsoft Graph documentation before the checklist is executed.
findings.fix: Verify the exact permission name against the Graph learningCourseActivities reference (the deck spec already carries the learn.microsoft.com URL) and correct lines 536-546 and 698 if needed.

findings.claim: Platform table claims (lines 207-215, 248-249): Viva Learning 'Native GCC / GCC High'; KnowBe4/Proofpoint 'FedRAMP Moderate authorized'; SANS 'FedRAMP-authorized'; Attack Simulator 'included in M365 E5 GCC' (Defender for Office 365 Plan 2); DoD Cyber Awareness Challenge 'GCC accessible' with ATCTS records
findings.problem: Marketplace-authorization, GCC-availability, and licensing-inclusion claims about external products; none verifiable in-repo and all procurement-load-bearing. The book's own guardrail ('verify Viva Learning GCC feature parity at time of deployment') covers Viva only — the FedRAMP-authorization claims for KnowBe4/Proofpoint/SANS carry no equivalent verify-at-procurement caveat.
findings.fix: Add a table footnote: 'Authorization status and GCC availability per vendor claim — verify on the FedRAMP Marketplace and in the current GCC service description at procurement time' (the deck's closing slide already says this; the qmd table does not).

findings.claim: "Microsoft has retired other Viva components (Viva Goals, December 2025; Viva Topics, February 2025) while redirecting investment toward Copilot"
findings.problem: External vendor-roadmap dates with no in-repo source and no 'Vendor sources:' link in the qmd (the series spec requires vendor claims to carry source links). Not judging true/false — needs the Microsoft retirement announcements cited.
findings.fix: Add the two Microsoft message-center/learn retirement announcement URLs alongside the claim.

findings.claim: Insider Threat Awareness module content: "Behavioral indicators, reporting obligations, DISA Insider Threat program" with driver EO 13587
findings.problem: DISA's insider-threat program is a DoD program; this book's context is SSA (civilian, GCC Moderate). EO 13587 established the National Insider Threat Task Force (NITTF) minimum standards, which is the applicable civilian-agency anchor. Citing DISA in an SSA training module is a wrong-community reference a reviewer would flag.
findings.fix: Replace 'DISA Insider Threat program' with 'NITTF minimum standards / agency insider-threat program (EO 13587)'.

findings.claim: Title column: AT-2(2) = 'Insider Threat Awareness' (lines 125, 580); AT-3(5) = 'Processing PII' (line 128)
findings.problem: Catalog SSOT (v5.2.0) titles are AT-2(2) 'Insider Threat' and AT-3(5) 'Processing Personally Identifiable Information'. Minor, but these sit in a Title column presented as official control titles, and the same 'Insider Threat Awareness' rendering is in the deck spec (slide 14).
findings.fix: Use the exact catalog titles in Title columns; keep descriptive phrasing in the mechanism column.

findings.claim: Export filename: Out-File "training-record-$(Get-Date -Format 'yyyyQq').json"
findings.problem: .NET custom date formats have no quarter specifier; 'Q' and 'q' are emitted as literal characters, so every export in a year writes to the same file 'training-record-2026Qq.json' rather than a per-quarter name — undermining the 'deterministic, repeatable, per-period record' claim.
findings.fix: Compute the quarter explicitly, e.g. "$((Get-Date).Year)Q$([math]::Ceiling((Get-Date).Month/3))".

findings.claim: Appendix A column 'CR26 Control' binds KSI-001..010 to KSI-IAM-MFA/LAB/PAC, KSI-SVC-EFR/SLP/VCM, KSI-MLA-MAU/ESH/DLP, KSI-023..025 to KSI-INR-IRR/MLE/NTA, and KSI-026..029 to KSI-RPL-BCP/BCT/DRP/DRT.
findings.problem: Contradicts AAN_CR26_Reconciliation.md (the in-repo CR26 diff this same book cites as authority). The reconciliation says IAM/SVC/MLA/CNA have ZERO indicator-ID bindings ('no indicator-ID binding' for KSI-001..010), and the real CR26 MLA indicators are ALA/EVC/LET/OSM/RVL — KSI-MLA-MAU, KSI-MLA-ESH, KSI-MLA-DLP do not exist in the 46-indicator list. For INR the mapped indicators are KSI-INR-AAR/RIR/RPI (not IRR/MLE/NTA) and for RPL they are KSI-RPL-ABO/ARP/RRO/TRC (not BCP/BCT/DRP/DRT). 17 of 29 rows in the table carry CR26 indicator IDs that are either fabricated or wrong; an assessor diffing this against the reconciliation file would reject the appendix.
findings.fix: Regenerate Appendix A from AAN_CR26_Reconciliation.md: use the 19 real mapped indicator IDs for the mapped rows, and mark KSI-001..010 as 'ScuBA baseline — no CR26 indicator-ID binding' instead of inventing IDs. Rename the column or annotate rows so unmapped rules never display a 'CR26 Control' value.

findings.claim: §2.5 POA&M status block says 'Satisfied : 29 (all 29 CR26 KSIs)' and §9 CA-2 row (line ~695) says the AR is 'the formal security assessment record for all 29 CR26 KSIs'.
findings.problem: Directly contradicts the book's own KSI-count reconciliation callout (lines 69-79) and AAN_CR26_Reconciliation.md: the 29 rules are the internal decomposition, CR26 has 46 indicators, and only 19/46 are explicitly mapped. Calling them '29 CR26 KSIs' in two load-bearing places (the POA&M evidence block and the CA-2 closure row) is exactly the conflation the callout was written to prevent.
findings.fix: Change both occurrences to 'all 29 internal KSI rules (see KSI-count reconciliation, §1.1)' or equivalent.

findings.claim: §5.1 states BOD 26-04 requires all federal agencies to (1) maintain an SBOM for all production software by December 7, 2026, (2) file a VDR per component, (3) file a VER for each CVE above CVSS 7.0, (4) demonstrate continuous SBOM monitoring; subtitle and preface item 3 repeat 'the December 7, 2026 SBOM + vendor disclosure'.
findings.problem: The deadline SSOT (aan-authority-deadlines.yml) characterizes BOD 26-04 as risk-based remediation: Aug 7, 2026 = agency vulnerability-management policies; Dec 7, 2026 = 'remediation timelines in force; FedRAMP VDR/VER mandatory adoption' (source: fedramp.gov notice 0014 — a FedRAMP/CSP action, not an agency SBOM filing). The spine's authority note is 'VDR/VER + risk-based remediation'. Neither SSOT supports an agency mandate to maintain/submit SBOMs to CISA by Dec 7, a per-component VDR filing duty, or a CVSS-7.0 VER threshold. The date itself matches the SSOT but the obligation attached to it is misdescribed — an ISSO checking the directive would find the requirement list unsupported.
findings.fix: Rewrite §5.1 (and the subtitle/preface framing) to match the SSOT: Dec 7, 2026 = BOD 26-04 remediation timelines in force and FedRAMP VDR/VER mandatory adoption for the CSOs SSA inherits; recast the SBOM/VDR/VER pipeline as SSA's supporting evidence (SR family + Vol IV Book 02), not as the directive's literal text. Source every stated obligation to the directive.

findings.claim: §2.3 AP theme table assigns KSI-017–019 to theme KSI-IAM and lists KSI-PIY as only KSI-020, KSI-021 (repeated in the fig-ato03 alt text).
findings.problem: Appendix A of this same book and AAN_CR26_Reconciliation.md both map KSI-017/018/019 to KSI-PIY indicators (KSI-PIY-GIV/RES/RIS). The AP theme table and the AR findings table in the same document disagree on which theme five rules belong to. Additionally KSI-002 appears in no theme row at all (rows cover 28 distinct rules, with KSI-008 double-listed under SVC and CNA), so the table does not account for all 29 rules it claims to organize.
findings.fix: Correct the theme table: KSI-PIY = KSI-017–021; KSI-IAM = KSI-001, 002, 003, 009 (per the ScuBA set); add KSI-002; regenerate fig-ato03 to match.

findings.claim: 'This is the nineteenth and final book in the Federal AAN series. The preceding eighteen books, spanning Volumes I–IV...'; §1.1 'delivered eighteen technical books'; §4.1 evidence component = 'the preceding eighteen books, Volumes I–IV'; §8.1 'Confirm all 19 books compiled'.
findings.problem: aan-compliance-spine.yml (book registry SSOT, dated 2026-07-13) registers 22 content books in Volumes I–IV besides this one — including Vol I Book 07 (Network Enforcement Substrate), Vol III Book 03 (Patch & Systems Management), Vol III Book 04 (Cloud-Native Posture), and Vol III Book 07 (Multi-Cloud Evidence Fabric) — plus Volumes 0 and V–IX. 'Final book' and the 18/19 counts are stale, and the §1.1 coverage table and §4.1 package component index omit registered books that carry closures (e.g., SC-7/SC-8/IA-3 in book-net-enforce, CA-7 in book-evidence-fabric), so the authorization package as described is incomplete relative to the spine.
findings.fix: Re-anchor the preface, §1.1 table, §4.1 component index, and §8.1 checklist to the spine registry (or state explicitly that this book covers only the original 18-book core and name the exclusions); drop 'final book'.

findings.claim: Closing note: control closure claims are 'advisory pending formal ATO review by the FedRAMP Project Management Office and the Agency Authorizing Official.'
findings.problem: The preface (lines 34-35) states as a load-bearing scope decision: 'SSA is a consuming agency, not a cloud service provider: nothing in this package is submitted to the FedRAMP PMO.' The footer reintroduces FedRAMP PMO review of this very package — a direct contradiction on the package's fundamental authorization posture that a hostile reviewer would quote back immediately.
findings.fix: Footer should read 'pending independent security control assessment and acceptance by the SSA Authorizing Official' — remove the FedRAMP PMO.

findings.claim: 'Controls closed by this document: CA-2, CA-5, CA-6, CA-7, CA-7(1), CA-7(3), RA-3, SA-15' and the §9 closure table.
findings.problem: aan-compliance-spine.yml contains zero closure rows for book-19 (grep 'book: book-19' in closures: no matches). The spine is the declared SSOT from which 'Authorities Closed Here' tables are generated and drift-gated; this book's closure claims exist only in prose. (Spine notes closures are back-filled sequentially, but until book-19 rows exist the claim is unregistered and the CA-2/CA-5/CA-7 closures currently belong to book-sn-attestation and book-evidence-fabric.)
findings.fix: Back-fill book-19 closure rows (control, mechanism, gate, drivers, slot, ksi) in aan-compliance-spine.yml for CA-2, CA-5, CA-6, CA-7, CA-7(1), CA-7(3), RA-3, SA-15, then regenerate the authorities table.

findings.claim: §9 row: 'SA-15 | Development Process Standards'.
findings.problem: Official Rev 5 title per reference/nist-800-53r5-controls.json is 'Development Process, Standards, and Tools'. A truncated control title in the closure table is the kind of catalog mismatch a 3PAO flags.
findings.fix: Use the full title 'Development Process, Standards, and Tools'.

findings.claim: §7.2 residual-risk bullet: 'Physical security — AC-18/19, PE family (not in scope for cloud boundary)'.
findings.problem: Per the control catalog SSOT, AC-18 is 'Wireless Access' and AC-19 is 'Access Control for Mobile Devices' — neither is a physical-security control, and AC-19 is claimed as CLOSED by Vol I Book 02 in this book's own §1.1 table (and by book-net-enforce in the spine), so listing it as an out-of-scope residual risk is also self-contradictory.
findings.fix: Change the bullet to 'Physical security — PE family (inherited from the CSP data-center authorization)' and drop AC-18/19.

findings.claim: CA-7(1) closure: 'ScuBA assessment provides continuous independent M365 validation.'
findings.problem: Per §3.2's own activity matrix, ScuBAGear is run by the SSA ISSO — the system's own staff running a tool is not an independent assessment under CA-7(1) (Independent Assessment). The tool's baseline is external (CISA), but independence attaches to the assessor, not the rubric; the book itself elsewhere labels everything 'self-assessment pending independent SCA.'
findings.fix: Rest CA-7(1) closure solely on the planned independent SCA/3PAO engagement; describe ScuBA as agency self-assessment against an external baseline.

findings.claim: §4.1: 'the 20x KSI-evidence model replaces the 325-control audit binder'.
findings.problem: The 325 figure cannot be reproduced from any in-repo SSOT (the controls JSON is the full 1196-id catalog, not a Moderate baseline count), and the commonly published FedRAMP Rev 5 Moderate baseline count is 323. An assessor will check this number.
findings.fix: Either cite the exact FedRAMP Rev 5 Moderate baseline count with source, or drop the number ('the several-hundred-control audit binder').

findings.claim: §5.2.1 vexctl example: --status "affected" combined with --justification "component_not_present".
findings.problem: Self-contradictory on its face: 'component_not_present' is the justification for a NOT-affected determination (in OpenVEX, justifications attach to not_affected status). A VEX statement asserting a product is affected because the component is not present would be rejected by any consumer and undermines the pipeline's credibility as a worked example.
findings.fix: Use --status "not_affected" with --justification "component_not_present", or --status "affected" with no justification and an action statement.

findings.claim: §3.4 references: 'Vol IV Book 05 §3 IR Drill Cadence', 'Vol IV Book 01 §4 Tabletop Calendar', 'Vol IV Book 02 §5 VDR Pipeline'.
findings.problem: Checked against the target books' numbered headings: Book 05 §3 is 'Dimension 1 — General Security Awareness Training (AT-2)' (IR/DR training is §6, Dimension 4); Book 02 §5 is 'Vendor Disclosure Matrix' (the VDR section is §3, the pipeline §2). The Book 01 §4 reference is likewise unverifiable against its headings. Dangling section citations in a ConMon procedure table will fail an evidence walkthrough.
findings.fix: Correct the three section numbers/titles against the current target books, or cite by section title only.

findings.claim: §5.2.2: VDR/VER submissions go to sbom@cisa.dhs.gov, or the 'CISA VEX Portal', with subject-line format '[AGENCY] BOD-26-04 VDR Submission — ...'.
findings.problem: The submission email address, the existence of a 'CISA VEX Portal', and the mandated subject-line format appear in no in-repo SSOT and are presented as operational fact. If an ISSO mails the wrong channel on the Dec 7 deadline, this document is the cause. Not judging true/false — flagging for verification against the actual directive/CISA guidance.
findings.fix: Verify the submission channel against CISA's published BOD 26-04 implementation guidance and cite it; until then mark the channel as 'per CISA guidance at submission time'.

findings.claim: CA-7(3) titled 'Trend Analysis' (§3.6 heading and §9 table).
findings.problem: Official Rev 5 title per the catalog SSOT is 'Trend Analyses' (plural).
findings.fix: Change to 'Trend Analyses'.

findings.claim: SA-15 closure cites 'the uiao CI/CD gate (ruff, mypy, pytest 4768 tests)'.
findings.problem: A hard-coded test count is unreproducible from the document and drifts with every commit; it will be wrong by assessment time.
findings.fix: Say 'the full pytest suite (count recorded in the CI run artifact)' or bind the number to a generated artifact.

findings.claim: "Volume VII proved that ServiceNow can operate compliance drift as owned, evidenced work."
findings.problem: "Proved" asserts a completed operational demonstration, but Volume VII (and this whole series) is a draft proposal that has not been deployed or reviewed — the file's own warning callout says so. Vol VII specifies/designs the coordination loop; nothing in the corpus records it running against a tenant. A 3PAO would treat "proved" as an evidence claim with no evidence.
findings.fix: Soften to design-level language, e.g. "Volume VII established the pattern for operating compliance drift as owned, evidenced work" or "Volume VII showed how ServiceNow can operate...".

findings.claim: "ServiceNow Government Cloud coordination hub ... holds FedRAMP High authorization"
findings.problem: Vendor authorization-level claim about an external product (ServiceNow Government Cloud's FedRAMP Marketplace status). Not judged true/false here; this is the single baselined High mention (aan-high-claim-baseline.yml count 1) and it correctly delegates the High-on-Moderate treatment to Vol VII Book 00 rather than claiming control inheritance — but the marketplace fact itself needs periodic verification against the FedRAMP Marketplace, and this file carries no Vendor sources link (sourcing lives, if anywhere, in Vol VII Book 00).
findings.fix: Ensure Vol VII Book 00's Authorization Boundary Treatment section carries (or gains) a Vendor sources link to the FedRAMP Marketplace listing so this delegated claim has a verification anchor; no change needed in this file beyond confirming the delegation target is sourced.

findings.claim: The 'Authorities Closed Here' table (claimed 'Generated from the compliance spine... not hand-edited here') lists exactly three closures for this book: AC-2, AC-6, IA-5.
findings.problem: aan-compliance-spine.yml records FOUR closures for book-day2-helpdesk — AC-2, AC-3 (Access Enforcement, the Conditional-Access-exception mechanism), AC-6, IA-5. Running 'python render_authorities_table.py --book book-day2-helpdesk' produces the 4-row table, and the committed partial authorities/authorities-book-day2-helpdesk.md already contains the AC-3 row. The .qmd's embedded copy is stale, and it contradicts the book's own catalog table (line 47), which maps the Conditional-Access-exception item to AC-3. The existing drift gate (aan-authorities-drift.yml) only checks the authorities/ partials against the spine, not the copy embedded in the .qmd, so this drift is un-gated. A reviewer reconciling the book against the spine sees a claimed spine-generated table missing a control the book itself invokes.
findings.fix: Replace the embedded table block (the '<!-- authorities:book-day2-helpdesk -->' block) with the fresh output of 'python render_authorities_table.py --book book-day2-helpdesk', which adds the AC-3 | Access Enforcement row.

findings.claim: 'Repeated unlocks are a Vol VII Book 02 detection signal' (catalog table, Account unlock row; also echoed in servicenow-day2/helpdesk-control-map.json note 'Vol VII Book 02 detection signal (lockout/spray)').
findings.problem: Vol VII Book 02 (M365 Control Compliance Automation) contains no unlock, lockout, or password-spray detection content — grep finds zero matches. The spray/lockout detection actually lives in the Vol VI Book 03 detection library (impl/detection-rules/03-password-spray-lowandslow.yaml, rule '03-password-spray-lowandslow', controls SI-4/AC-7). A reader following the pointer finds no such signal in the cited book.
findings.fix: Point the Account-unlock note at Vol VI Book 03 (detection engineering / rule 03-password-spray-lowandslow) instead of Vol VII Book 02, in both the .qmd catalog table and the matching note in servicenow-day2/helpdesk-control-map.json.

findings.claim: Honest Limits: 'a standing global administrator can still act out of band — Vol VII Book 03 detections and access reviews catch that.'
findings.problem: Vol VII Book 03 is the AZURE control-compliance book (Azure Policy / Defender / Update Manager). The surface this catalog governs is Entra/M365 via Graph; out-of-band changes on that surface are caught by the Vol VII Book 02 M365 drift loop (and/or the Vol VI Book 03 detection library). Vol VII Book 03 contains no detection of out-of-band Entra/tenant-admin activity. The reference also sits oddly against line 44, which sends detection signals to Book 02 — the file points 'detections' at two different Vol VII books, neither of which is the detections book.
findings.fix: Change the reference to Vol VII Book 02 (M365 loop detects out-of-band Entra drift) and/or Vol VI Book 03 for the analytic detections; keep access reviews with Vol VII Book 02.

findings.claim: 'a weak SSPR policy is a Vol VI Book 02 configuration concern, not a catalog fix.'
findings.problem: Vol VI Book 02 (Identity & Access as Code) never mentions SSPR or the tenant authentication-methods policy; its as-code elements are Conditional Access, PIM, 802.1X profiles, and certificate lifecycle. The pointer is directionally plausible (identity policy as code) but a reader looking for SSPR/authentication-method policy guidance in that book finds nothing.
findings.fix: Either add authentication-methods/SSPR policy to Vol VI Book 02's as-code scope, or soften the pointer here (e.g. 'a tenant identity-policy concern (Vol VI Book 02 pattern)').

findings.claim: 'Multiplied across a week, that is the largest continuous source of control erosion in the estate.'
findings.problem: 'Largest' is an unquantified superlative presented as fact with no measurement, citation, or derivation anywhere in the series. A hostile reviewer asks 'largest by what metric, measured where?'
findings.fix: Soften to 'one of the largest' / 'a continuous, high-volume source of control erosion', or cite a volume metric if one exists.

findings.claim: Closure Necessity callout: "Volume VI proves the mechanism: landing zones expressed as reviewable source close CM-2/CM-3/CM-6."
findings.problem: The spine (aan-compliance-spine.yml) assigns NO control closures to any Vol VI book — Vol VI is the implementation layer with zero closure rows. CM-2 is closed by book-patch-sysmgmt and by THIS book (book-day2-landingzone); CM-3 by book-sn-cmdb/book-sn-saas/book-ddi-servicenow/book-day2-landingzone/book-day2-telephony; CM-6 by book-patch-sysmgmt and book-cloudnative-posture. Vol VI Book 01 itself (Vol_VI_Book_01_FedAAN_Landing_Zone_Network_as_Code.qmd) never mentions CM-2, CM-3, or CM-6 — its closure claims are CM-8 and SC-20/21/22. The sentence also undercuts this book's own generated table, which is where CM-2/CM-3 landing-zone closure actually lives.
findings.fix: Rephrase to match the spine: Vol VI Book 01 provides the reviewable-source mechanism (its own claims are CM-8 / SC-20/21/22); CM-2/CM-3 closure for landing zones happens HERE via the governed front door. Drop CM-6 or attribute drift/settings to Vol VII Book 03 / book-patch-sysmgmt where the spine closes it.

findings.claim: Series Context: "The infrastructure-as-code exists (Vol VI Book 01, `infoblox-ddi-book/azure-alz-automation/`)".
findings.problem: Per the spine, `infoblox-ddi-book/azure-alz-automation` is the kit for Vol VIII Book 01 (book-ddi-azure, kit-ddi-lz-azure), not Vol VI Book 01. Vol VI Book 01's source is Vol_VI_Book_01_FedAAN_Landing_Zone_Network_as_Code.qmd, which never references azure-alz-automation. Pairing the Vol VI book reference with the Vol VIII kit path sends a reviewer to the wrong artifact.
findings.fix: Either cite Vol VI Book 01 alone (the Landing Zone & Network as Code book) or cite Vol VIII Book 01 with the azure-alz-automation path; if both IaC sources are meant, list them as two distinct references.

findings.claim: "the exact pattern the DDI ServiceNow app already proves" (line 31) and "already implements this loop" (line 52); Provenance calls ServiceNow/CPG/Terraform/ALZ "deployed examples" (line 89).
findings.problem: The referenced artifact (infoblox-ddi-book/servicenow-app/) is an in-repo scoped-app kit — catalog, Flow, Script Includes, ATF, update-set spec, plus mockups — attached to a corpus whose own banner says draft, not reviewed or approved. There is no deployment record or assessment evidence in-repo that the loop has been exercised, so "proves" and "deployed" are assertions a 3PAO cannot trace to evidence.
findings.fix: Soften to what is supported: the DDI app "specifies/implements this loop as a buildable scoped-app kit (catalog, Flow, Script Includes, ATF, update set)" — keep 'proves' for after a deployment/ATF-run evidence artifact exists.

findings.claim: Vendor capability claims: "The CPG Terraform Connector runs a speculative plan the approver reviews" (lines 35, 41), "the Service Graph Connector reconciles to the CMDB" (line 52), MID-Server validation gate (line 52).
findings.problem: These are specific ServiceNow product-capability claims (CPG Terraform Connector speculative-plan support, Service Graph Connector CMDB reconciliation) that require verification against vendor documentation, and the series authoring spec requires 'Vendor sources:' links for vendor claims — this file carries none. Not judging the claims true or false; they are consistent with the DDI book corpus but unsourced here.
findings.fix: Add a 'Vendor sources:' block (ServiceNow CPG Terraform Connector and Service Graph Connector docs pages) per the Federal_AAN_Series_Authoring_Spec convention, or point explicitly to the Vol VIII book section that carries the vendor sources.

findings.claim: Figure/fig-alt describes a "five-step pipeline" ending at Reconcile; the table below enumerates SIX steps (adding "6. Close" with CM-3/AU-2); the intro pattern (line 31) lists SEVEN stages including a distinct validation gate.
findings.problem: Three different step counts for the same loop within one short document. A reviewer walking the figure against the table will ask where the validation gate and Close/evidence step went in the diagram, and which enumeration is authoritative.
findings.fix: Align the enumerations: either regenerate the figure with six steps (adding Close/validation-gate) or state in the caption that the figure folds validate+close into Reconcile. Optionally note that CM-5 (step 2) and AU-2 (step 6) are referenced-not-closed here — they are closed by Vol VIII Book 07 (book-ddi-servicenow) per the spine — so the loop table and the Authorities Closed Here table don't appear to disagree.

findings.claim: Teams is an M365 workload with a CISA SCuBA secure-configuration baseline covering "external access, meeting policies, app permissions, federation" (also asserted at line 29).
findings.problem: The existence of a Teams SCuBA baseline is well established and the CISA SCuBA project page is cited, but the specific enumeration of the four policy areas it covers is a claim about the content of an external CISA document that is not captured in any in-repo SSOT; the baseline's policy groups can change between SCuBA releases.
findings.fix: Verify the four named policy areas against the current CISA SCuBA Microsoft Teams Secure Configuration Baseline release, or soften to "e.g." phrasing so the list is illustrative rather than exhaustive.

findings.claim: The embedded 'Authorities Closed Here' table (marked 'generated from aan-compliance-spine.yml; do not hand-edit') lists three controls: AC-6, IA-5(2), SC-17.
findings.problem: The spine (aan-compliance-spine.yml, book-day2-appreg block, lines 374-378) assigns FOUR controls to this book, including AC-2 (Account Management). The committed partial authorities/authorities-book-day2-appreg.md contains the AC-2 row; the .qmd's embedded copy is stale and missing it. This .qmd is NOT in the aan-authorities-drift.yml workflow path list, so the drift gate does not cover this embed — the staleness is ungated, not already-gated. A reviewer diffing the book against the registry sees the book under-reporting its own closure set.
findings.fix: Re-run `python render_authorities_table.py --book book-day2-appreg` and replace the embedded table (adds the AC-2 row); consider adding this .qmd to the aan-authorities-drift workflow paths or embedding via include of the authorities/ partial.

findings.claim: "This book governs the whole lifecycle as catalog work, closing IA-5(2), SC-17, and AC-6..."
findings.problem: Hand-written prose omits AC-2, which the spine assigns to this book (mechanism: app registrations as machine JML with governed request and attestation-driven retirement). The omission is internally inconsistent too: the book's own lifecycle table cites AC-2 at stage 1, and the entire 'App Registrations Are Machine JML' section is the AC-2 mechanism.
findings.fix: Change to "closing AC-2, IA-5(2), SC-17, and AC-6".

findings.claim: The lifecycle table defines SIX stages (Request, Approve, Consent, Credential, Rotate, Attest) and the text says 'Attestation (stage 6)'.
findings.problem: The subtitle, the Series Context callout, the figure, and the fig-alt all describe a FIVE-step lifecycle (request, consent, credential, rotate, attest — the fig-alt explicitly says 'five-step pipeline' with 'Step 5 Attest'). A hostile reviewer asks which is the governed process of record: the 5-step figure or the 6-stage table. Stage numbering in prose ('stage 6') matches the table but contradicts the committed diagram.
findings.fix: Pick one shape: either fold Approve into Consent in the table (5 stages, matching the figure) or note in the figure caption that Approve is shown merged into the Consent step.

findings.claim: App registrations are 'the largest source of long-lived-secret and over-consent risk in an Entra estate.'
findings.problem: Superlative risk-ranking asserted with no source, dataset, or in-repo register backing it; nothing in the spine or the series' gap registers ranks Entra risk sources. 'A large source' is defensible from the mechanism argument; 'the largest' is not reproducible.
findings.fix: Soften to 'one of the largest sources' or 'a dominant source', or cite a source if one exists.

findings.claim: Credential stage: 'a short-lived certificate (ACME)' with 'automated rotation before expiry; the app never depends on a human remembering' (also asserted as the IA-5(2) closing mechanism and as 'deployed examples' in Provenance).
findings.problem: Entra app registrations do not natively auto-rotate certificate credentials; the 'never depends on a human' guarantee rests on external ACME/rotation tooling and Graph automation whose capability cannot be verified from the repo. The book partially acknowledges this ('this book governs the workflow, not the CA') but the lifecycle table states the rotation guarantee unconditionally. Not judged true or false — flagged as a claim a 3PAO would ask to see demonstrated.
findings.fix: Anchor the rotation claim to the named mechanism (the Vol I Book 03 / Vol VI Book 02 CA + rotation pipeline) rather than stating it as an unconditional property, or add an evidence pointer.

findings.claim: Book 02 (Network Access Control 802.1X) is characterized as 'Device identity at the physical port (IA-3)' (also in the fig-alt at line 56).
findings.problem: The spine's only registered IA-3 closure is at book-net-enforce (Vol I Book 07), with mechanism '802.1X authenticator + NAC at the port' — essentially the mechanism this overview assigns to Book 02. Book 02 has zero closure entries in the spine (closures are back-filled sequentially per the spine header, so this is a known-WIP tension, not a hard contradiction — controls can also legitimately appear under multiple books, as SC-7 already does).
findings.fix: When Book 02's closures are back-filled into aan-compliance-spine.yml, either add an IA-3 entry for book-02 (design/doctrine plane) alongside book-net-enforce's gear-gate entry, or adjust the Book 02 role text here to note the accreditation-gated IA-3 closure lands at Book 07.

findings.claim: 'transport + edge enforcement (Vol I Books 06–07) are where the customer-owned half of SC-7/SC-8 is closed'
findings.problem: The spine registers SC-7, SC-7(8), SC-8, and SC-8(1) closures only at book-net-enforce (Book 07); book-06 (Federal Telecommunications Modernization) currently has no closure entries at all, so the 'Books 06–07' joint closure attribution cannot be reproduced from the SSOT as written. Same back-fill caveat as above.
findings.fix: Either back-fill book-06 SC-8 (encrypted SD-WAN/SASE overlay transport) entries into the spine, or narrow this sentence to attribute the registered closures to Book 07 with Book 06 as the transport substrate.

findings.claim: "SSA inherits both the InfoBlox CSO (FR2017257053) and the AWS GovCloud infrastructure authorization — layered FedRAMP coverage" (AWS GovCloud cited with its FedRAMP High authorization).
findings.problem: Load-bearing inheritance claim built on a FedRAMP High authorization. An agency consuming a SaaS CSO does not separately inherit the underlying IaaS authorization; AWS GovCloud is a leveraged authorization inside InfoBlox's own package, and its High baseline confers nothing extra to SSA's Moderate boundary. A 3PAO would reject 'layered FedRAMP coverage' as a shared-responsibility misstatement. (This line is within the 5-mention gate baseline, but the task directs reporting High mentions used as inheritance claims.)
findings.fix: Rewrite: under Path A SSA inherits only from the InfoBlox CSO at Moderate; note that InfoBlox leverages AWS GovCloud within its own authorization package — no second inheritance accrues to SSA.

findings.claim: "The FedRAMP authorization boundary is defined by IP address ranges. InfoBlox IPAM *is* the authoritative record of every IP inside the boundary. The CM-8 IP inventory export *is* the boundary IP list — no separate reconciliation required."
findings.problem: Factually wrong (a FedRAMP boundary is defined by components, services, interconnections, and data flows, not IP ranges — SaaS components and external services have no agency IP) and directly contradicted by the file's own CMDB section: line 709 says InfoBlox 'does not satisfy the full control', R-04 says boundary membership must be carried in the CMDB (i.e., IPAM does not know it), and Phase 1 (line 824) explicitly reconciles the export against the CMDB.
findings.fix: Restate Layer 1 as: the IPAM export is the authoritative address-layer input to the boundary inventory, which is reconciled with the CMDB — consistent with sec-cmdb; drop 'no separate reconciliation required'.

findings.claim: NIST mapping table 'Satisfies' column cites SI-3(1) (line 549) and SC-20(1) (line 536) as satisfied enhancements.
findings.problem: Both enhancements are WITHDRAWN in 800-53 Rev 5: SI-3(1) Central Management was incorporated into PL-9, and SC-20(1) Child Subspaces was incorporated into SC-20. The in-repo catalog JSON records the ids/titles but not withdrawal status; per the official Rev 5 catalog these cannot be 'satisfied', and a 3PAO would reject evidence mapped to withdrawn enhancements.
findings.fix: Change 'SI-3, SI-3(1)' to 'SI-3' and 'SC-20, SC-20(1)' to 'SC-20'; consider extending the reference JSON to carry withdrawn status so the gate can catch this class.

findings.claim: "A single InfoBlox deployment provides evidence for 16 controls..."
findings.problem: The count cannot be reproduced from the table that follows: it has 15 rows, 17 distinct base controls in the Satisfies column, and 22 distinct control identifiers including enhancements. No counting method yields 16.
findings.fix: Recount after fixing the withdrawn enhancements and state the counting basis (e.g., '15 control rows covering N distinct Rev 5 identifiers').

findings.claim: "The subdomain strategy adds three controls to the NIST mapping in Section @sec-nist" (SC-22, AC-4, SA-9).
findings.problem: Two of the three (SC-22, line 538; SA-9, line 543) already appear in the sec-nist mapping table. Only AC-4 is actually new, so the 'adds three controls' arithmetic is internally contradictory.
findings.fix: Say the namespace design adds AC-4 and deepens the existing SC-22 and SA-9 rows, or restructure the table as 'contributions' rather than additions.

findings.claim: Phase 6: "Configure all eight FedRAMP control evidence exports as scheduled reports."
findings.problem: The FedRAMP Moderate evidence table (sec-fedramp-moderate) has 7 rows covering 9 controls (SC-20, SC-21, CM-8, IA-5(2), AU-2, AU-12, IR-4, SA-9, SC-22). Neither counting method yields eight.
findings.fix: Align the number with the evidence table ('all seven evidence exports' or 'the nine mapped controls') or name the eighth export.

findings.claim: Callout "Closure Necessity — SC-20 / SC-21 / SC-22 (authoritative DNS)" presents all three as necessity anchors of this book.
findings.problem: aan-compliance-spine.yml registers book-01's closures as SC-20 and SC-21 only (both necessity: true, with alternative rebuttals); SC-22 is closed at book-ddi-xplat (Vol VIII) with necessity: false. Extending the necessity claim to SC-22 in prose contradicts the closure registry.
findings.fix: Limit the necessity callout to SC-20/SC-21 and reference SC-22's architecture treatment in Vol VIII, or register an SC-22 necessity row for book-01 in the spine (author decision).

findings.claim: "InfoBlox polls the Microsoft 365 IP & URL Web Service API daily ... closing the boundary gap window to minutes" (also line 271: "all four update within minutes of Microsoft's API publishing the change").
findings.problem: A daily poll bounds the gap window at up to ~24 hours after Microsoft publishes, not minutes. 'Minutes' is only true relative to the poll, not to publication. A hostile reviewer will time-line this.
findings.fix: State the honest bound: 'within minutes of the next daily poll — a worst-case window of 24 hours, versus 7+ days manually', or specify a shorter poll interval.

findings.claim: "Every DNS query from every workload passes through the InfoBlox Grid Member (because all VPC/VNet/NSX-T DHCP Options point to it)."
findings.problem: DHCP-delivered resolver settings do not bind workloads with statically configured resolvers, hardcoded DoH clients, or direct-to-IP traffic. The parenthetical mechanism does not support 'every'; AU-12 'every external communication visible in DNS logs' (line 627) inherits the same gap. No compensating egress control (e.g., blocking outbound 53/853/443-DoH to non-Grid resolvers) is cited here.
findings.fix: Qualify the claim and name the enforcement mechanism that makes it true (NSG/SG egress rules restricting DNS to Grid Members), or cross-reference the book that carries it.

findings.claim: "Only IP host records within the InfoBlox IPAM database can receive certificates via SCEP/EST enrollment automation. Certificate possession = boundary membership — a powerful assertion for boundary documentation and IA-9 satisfaction."
findings.problem: The equivalence only holds for certificates issued through this one automation path; the same CAs (ADCS, Key Vault, ACM PCA) issue certificates through other channels, so certificate possession does not prove boundary membership and the IA-9 satisfaction claim is unsupported as stated.
findings.fix: Scope the claim to 'certificates issued via the Grid-triggered SCEP/EST pipeline' and drop the unqualified possession=membership equivalence.

findings.claim: Qualys GAI/VMDR and Tenable.sc listed as "FedRAMP Moderate (JAB P-ATO)" (lines 764-765).
findings.problem: The JAB was dissolved in 2024 and the CR26-era marketplace no longer issues JAB P-ATO designations, so the label is stale on its face; current authorization status/designation for both products requires FedRAMP Marketplace verification (not judged true/false here).
findings.fix: Replace 'JAB P-ATO' with the current marketplace designation at verification time, matching the 'verify at procurement' caveat used for the other rows.

findings.claim: Infoblox Government Cloud CSO FR2017257053, FedRAMP Moderate, hosted on AWS GovCloud; "one of a small number of DDI platforms with its own FedRAMP Moderate CSO authorization" (line 59).
findings.problem: Marketplace listing id, baseline, hosting, and the 'small number' market claim are external facts the file itself flags for verification; they anchor the Path A inheritance argument, so they must be confirmed against the FedRAMP Marketplace before this document is used.
findings.fix: Verify the CSO listing, impact level, and service model on the Marketplace and record the verification date; soften or source the 'small number' claim.

findings.claim: VCF 9.1 (released May 2026) "makes InfoBlox the native, default IPAM backend for VMware Cloud Foundation" (intro at line 139 says 'first-class feature').
findings.problem: Vendor claim. 'Default IPAM backend' is stronger than 'native integration' and than what the cited VMware blog title suggests ('seamless DDI integration'); release date and default-status need verification against the VMware/Broadcom source.
findings.fix: Verify against the linked VMware blog/TechDocs; if the source says 'supported integration', downgrade 'default' accordingly and add the vendor-sources link inline per the series authoring spec.

findings.claim: "RPZ with CISA Protective DNS feed" (also lines 571, 609 fig-alt, 796) — CISA Protective DNS consumed as an RPZ feed inside agency-operated InfoBlox.
findings.problem: CISA's Protective DNS is delivered to agencies as a recursive resolver service; whether its threat data is separately consumable as an RPZ feed loaded into an agency's own Grid is an external fact that changes the SC-21 evidence story if wrong.
findings.fix: Verify the consumption model with CISA/InfoBlox documentation; if Protective DNS is resolver-only, restate as 'forwarding to CISA Protective DNS plus commercial RPZ feeds (TIDE)'.

findings.claim: "InfoBlox and Microsoft have a formal Azure Technology Alliance Partnership with six distinct integration points", incl. bidirectional TIDE↔MDTI IOC sharing and a first-party Sentinel content pack; InfoBlox "available on the Oracle Cloud Marketplace" (line 63); DoH/DoT on Grid Members (line 661).
findings.problem: Vendor-relationship and product-capability claims with no 'Vendor sources:' links, which the series authoring spec (Federal_AAN_Series_Authoring_Spec.md) requires for vendor claims; the References table covers none of the Microsoft-partnership or Oracle Marketplace assertions.
findings.fix: Add vendor source links for each partnership/integration claim or mark them pending verification.

findings.claim: Table 'FedRAMP 20x KSI Automation' presents rows like "All DNS traffic encrypted or integrity-protected" and "No CIDR overlap between environments" as FedRAMP 20x KSIs.
findings.problem: These are paraphrases not traceable to any CR26 KSI id (the real CR26 registry is a fixed set of named KSI indicators); a reviewer asked 'which KSI is that?' cannot map any row. Presenting invented indicator text under the header 'FedRAMP 20x KSI' overstates alignment.
findings.fix: Either cite the actual KSI ids each row supports (e.g., KSI-CNA-xx) from the CR26 machine-readable rules, or retitle the column 'KSI-supporting automation' and say which KSI family each row evidences.

findings.claim: SC-22 titled "Architecture and Provisioning for Name/Address Resolution".
findings.problem: Official Rev 5 title in the catalog SSOT is "Architecture and Provisioning for Name/Address Resolution Service" — the final word is dropped.
findings.fix: Append 'Service' to the SC-22 title.

findings.claim: Closing FOUO banner is dated "June 29, 2026".
findings.problem: Contradicts the document's Date Code (2026-07-08 16:07 ET) in the header and draft callout — two different dates on the same artifact.
findings.fix: Update the footer banner to the current Date Code.

findings.claim: "When a workload decommissions, all three [IP, DNS, cert] are revoked atomically."
findings.problem: IPAM release, DNS deletion, and CA revocation span three systems with no transactional mechanism named; 'atomically' is a stronger guarantee than the described Terraform/WAPI pipeline provides (partial failure leaves orphans).
findings.fix: Say 'revoked in a single automated pipeline' and note the reconciliation check that catches partial failures.

findings.claim: "Vol I Book 03 of the 19-part Federal Application-Aware Networking series" (also line 442 "under the 19-part restructure", line 447 heading "Vol I Book 03 of 19", line 475 footer "Vol I Book 03 of 19").
findings.problem: The count 19 cannot be reproduced from the spine SSOT (aan-compliance-spine.yml): the registry now holds 10 volumes (0 through IX) with ~67 registered books, and even the numbered content core spans target slots 01-21 (23 content books after book-net-enforce, book-patch-sysmgmt, book-cloudnative-posture, book-evidence-fabric were added). Across the whole corpus only this book (4 occurrences) and Vol I Book 04 (2) still say "19-part" — every other book dropped it, so it is stale, not a series convention.
findings.fix: Replace "19-part" / "of 19" with a spine-derived formulation (e.g. name the volume structure, or cite the series without a hard book count) in all four locations, matching what the rest of the corpus does.

findings.claim: "The controls this document closes — IA-5(2), SC-12, SC-17, IA-2(1), IA-2(2) — have no alternate closure path" (exec summary), plus the hand-authored closure table at lines 423-431 and three Closure Necessity blockquotes.
findings.problem: The spine (the declared SSOT for every closure claim; closures carry an explicit necessity flag and alternative_rebuttal) registers ZERO closures for book-03. Worse for the "no alternate closure path" framing: IA-5(2) and SC-17 ARE registered in the spine as closed by other books (book-sn-saas / Vol VII Book 06 line 336-338, and book-day2-appreg / Vol IX Book 03 line 376-377), while SC-12, IA-2(1), IA-2(2) appear nowhere in the closures section. The spine header notes closures are being back-filled sequentially, so absence may be pending work — but until book-03 rows exist (with necessity flags and rebuttals), a 3PAO diffing this book's closure claims against the registry finds an unregistered 5-control closure claim and two controls the registry attributes elsewhere.
findings.fix: Back-fill book-03 closure rows in aan-compliance-spine.yml for IA-5(2), SC-12, SC-17, IA-2(1), IA-2(2) with necessity: true and alternative_rebuttal text (the book already contains the rebuttal prose), and reconcile scope wording so the narrower IA-5(2)/SC-17 closures in Vol VII/IX read as applications of this book's mechanism rather than alternates.

findings.claim: Kerberos assumes "a domain controller is reachable within sub-5 ms round-trip" (also line 126 "Sub-5 ms round-trip assumption to the KDC", line 270 "The sub-5 ms location binding is gone").
findings.problem: RFC 4120 (which the book itself cites) imposes a clock-skew bound (the five-minute time binding, correctly stated) but NO latency requirement; "sub-5 ms" is not a protocol property and cannot be checked against protocol behavior. This matters because the property table introduces itself with "each row is checkable against protocol behavior, which is what the series' consistency rules require of every claim" — a hostile reviewer checks this row against RFC 4120 and finds nothing. It reads as a derived number with no derivation.
findings.fix: Either soften to what is defensible ("engineered for flat-LAN latencies; timeout and fallback behavior degrades sharply as KDC round-trip grows") or attribute the 5 ms figure to its actual source (e.g. a Vol I Book 05 latency analysis or vendor guidance) instead of presenting it as a Kerberos assumption.

findings.claim: CA/Browser Forum "has adopted a schedule that reduces the maximum validity of publicly trusted TLS certificates from 398 days stepwise down to 47 days by 2029, with the first reductions already in force in 2026" (also exec summary line 53); and line 150: public CAs "are required by the CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements to check and honor CAA at issuance time".
findings.problem: These are external industry-body claims covered by no in-repo SSOT (the deadline registry is federal-only), yet they are load-bearing: the entire "manual certificate management is ending by arithmetic" argument and the 34-minute renewal calculation hang on the 47-day/2029 schedule. The document cites no source for the CA/B Forum ballot or the Baseline Requirements CAA obligation, contrary to the series' own sourcing convention for external claims. Not judging the claims true or false — flagging that they need a verifiable citation.
findings.fix: Add source citations (CA/Browser Forum ballot for the lifetime schedule; Baseline Requirements section for the CAA checking obligation) at both the exec-summary and body occurrences, per the series' external-source convention.

findings.claim: "For readers tracking the five doctrine themes across the series" — the table lists Themes A through E only.
findings.problem: The spine explicitly defines a Theme F ("Accreditation gates (Theme F)", aan-compliance-spine.yml line 99), and the comprehensive-rebuild doctrine added it series-wide. A reviewer cross-checking the doctrine table against the spine finds six themes, not five — and the omission is not neutral here, since Theme F (which accreditation gate carries each control's evidence) is exactly the column this book's hand-authored closure table lacks.
findings.fix: Retitle to the current theme count and add a Theme F row stating how the accreditation-gate doctrine lands in this book (e.g. FIPS 140-validated HSMs and FedRAMP-authorized identity services as the gates for the trust fabric).

findings.claim: "This document is Vol I Book 04 of the 19-part Federal Application-Aware Networking series" (line 39); "Under the 19-part restructure" (line 500); "This part completes the substrate on which the fifteen parts that follow are built" (line 507).
findings.problem: Contradicts the spine registry (aan-compliance-spine.yml): the series is now 9 named volumes; the prose corpus alone has 23 numbered content books (book-01..book-19 plus back-fill books Vol I Book 07, Vol III Books 03/04/07), so neither "19-part" nor "fifteen parts that follow" is reproducible. The spine header explicitly says to cross-reference books by id/title, never by hardcoded number, until the Phase G renumber. Only Books 03 and 04 still carry the stale "19-part" phrase — Book 00 does not.
findings.fix: Replace "19-part" with a count-free phrase (e.g. "the Federal Application-Aware Networking series") and rephrase "the fifteen parts that follow" as "the parts that follow" (or derive the count from the spine at render time). Same fix at lines 39, 500, and 507. Also fix the sibling occurrences in Vol_I_Book_03.

findings.claim: Exec summary: the six controls "have no alternate closure path" (line 57); doctrine table Theme A: "AC-2/AC-2(1), PS-4, PS-5, IA-4, SI-12 each closed (or evidenced) by a mechanism with no alternative" (line 522).
findings.problem: The spine (aan-compliance-spine.yml line 392) records AC-2(1) with necessity: false and no alternative_rebuttal, while the other five book-04 rows are necessity: true. The book asserts closure-necessity for AC-2(1) that the spine — the registry a 3PAO would be shown — does not back, and the spine comment says its rebuttals were transcribed from this book's own table, so the two artifacts now disagree.
findings.fix: Either set necessity: true with an alternative_rebuttal for AC-2(1) in the spine (if the no-alternative argument is intended), or soften the book's exec-summary and Theme A language to exclude AC-2(1) from the no-alternative claim.

findings.claim: "For readers tracking the five doctrine themes across the series" — table lists Themes A–E only (lines 518–528).
findings.problem: The series doctrine now includes Theme F ("The Accreditation Substrate", Vol 0 Book 00 line 464; the spine's gates section is labeled "Accreditation gates (Theme F)"). Calling it "the five doctrine themes" contradicts the keystone and the spine. (Theme F may genuinely have no expression in this book, but the count is wrong.)
findings.fix: Change to "the six doctrine themes" and add a Theme F row (e.g. "the SaaS system of record sits behind an external authorization boundary — the FedRAMP gate, not NIAP/STIG, carries its evidence") or explicitly note Theme F does not land in this book.

findings.claim: "The Evidence Act (2018) and the Federal Data Strategy require that agency data trace to a single authoritative system of record for each data type, with documented lineage from source to decision."
findings.problem: Overstated statutory requirement. The Foundations for Evidence-Based Policymaking Act mandates data governance, CDOs, inventories, and open-data practices; the Federal Data Strategy treats authoritative data sources as a practice. Neither instrument literally "requires" a single authoritative system of record per data type with source-to-decision lineage. A hostile ISSO will ask for the section citation and not find one.
findings.fix: Soften to what the instruments actually direct (e.g. "establish data-governance and identify authoritative data assets — a direction only a designated system of record can satisfy"), or cite the specific provision if one exists.

findings.claim: "The verified operating numbers: throttling at 40 API calls per 5-second window; tenant daily caps of 2,000 calls per 24 hours (Entra ID P1/P2) or 6,000 (Entra ID Governance); batch payloads of up to 50 operations per call; Entra ID P1 as the licensing floor; ... three active provisioning agents for high availability" — plus "the spec's own correction history records that its first draft overstated the throttling envelope five-fold and was corrected on verification against the authoritative source."
findings.problem: These Microsoft platform limits are asserted as "verified against Microsoft Learn" but carry no vendor-source link (the series' own authoring spec requires "Vendor sources:" links for vendor claims), and the numbers appear nowhere else in the repo. The "correction history" of Spec2-D3.1 is not reproducible from any in-repo artifact — Spec2-D3.1 is referenced by name only (Book 00, conmon roadmap) with no spec file containing a correction record. Do not judge the numbers true/false; they require external verification against Microsoft Learn, and the provenance claim needs an in-repo anchor.
findings.fix: Add the Microsoft Learn URL(s) for the bulkUpload throttling/quota and provisioning-agent guidance next to the numbers, and either commit the Spec2-D3.1 spec (with its correction history) to the series folder or drop the correction-history sentence.

findings.claim: Oracle HCM Cloud is "the deployed instance" of OPM HRIT — SaaS delivered from an externally managed OCI tenancy, with a 2026 "SaaS delivery" milestone row (lines 135, 149, 163).
findings.problem: Load-bearing vendor/program claim about OPM's HCM platform selection and 2026 delivery that cannot be verified from any in-repo SSOT (the series' own conmon roadmap lists Workday Government Cloud and SAP SuccessFactors as alternates, and the book's caveat callout concedes vendor selections evolve). It anchors the fourth-landing-zone integration story, so a reviewer will probe it first. Not judging true/false — flagging for external verification against current OPM HRIT program status.
findings.fix: Keep the existing draft-proposal caveat but add an OPM/QSMO source citation for the platform selection, or restate as "the platform assumed for this architecture" rather than "the deployed instance" until externally confirmed.

findings.claim: OPM HRIT history table: CPDF 1972; e-Payroll consolidating 26 payroll providers to 4 (2002); HR Line of Business 2004; EHRI ~2010 replacing CPDF; OMB M-19-16 (April 2019) designating OPM the HR QSMO; QSMO marketplace opening 2021 (lines 141–151, 133).
findings.problem: External historical/program claims with no in-repo SSOT and no source links (the M-19-16 title and QSMO designation look right, but the 26-to-4 count, EHRI date, and marketplace-opening year are unverifiable from the repo). The in-file caveat callout mitigates but does not source them.
findings.fix: Add issuing-agency source links (OPM HRLOB/QSMO pages, M-19-16 PDF) to the timeline rows, matching the series' vendor-sources convention.

findings.claim: Microsoft feature-family claims: HR-driven provisioning is a "generally available, documented feature family"; prebuilt Workday/SAP SuccessFactors connectors; Graph bulkUpload accepting SCIM 2.0 with HTTP 202; parentDistinguishedName Switch-expression OU placement; employeeOrgData with costCenter/division; Lifecycle Workflows triggering off employeeHireDate/employeeLeaveDateTime (lines 264–292).
findings.problem: Vendor-capability claims consistent with Microsoft's documented architecture but not verifiable from any in-repo SSOT and carrying no "Vendor sources:" links as the series authoring spec requires. Not judging true/false.
findings.fix: Add Microsoft Learn links for HR-driven provisioning, API-driven inbound provisioning (cloud and on-prem AD targets), and Lifecycle Workflows at first mention.

findings.claim: Table row: "SI-3 Malware Protection"
findings.problem: Official SP 800-53 Rev 5 title (catalog v5.2.0, reference/nist-800-53r5-controls.json) is "Malicious Code Protection". A 3PAO checks titles against the catalog verbatim.
findings.fix: Rename to "SI-3 Malicious Code Protection".

findings.claim: "AU-2 / AU-12 Audit Events / Audit Record Generation" (also line ~499 in a table explicitly headed "NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Control")
findings.problem: "Audit Events" is the withdrawn Rev 4 title. The Rev 5 title of AU-2 per the catalog SSOT is "Event Logging". Citing the Rev 4 title under a Rev 5 header is factually wrong. AU-12 "Audit Record Generation" is correct.
findings.fix: Change AU-2's title to "Event Logging" in both tables (line ~259 and ~499).

findings.claim: Three rows labeled "Automated KSI: all DNS encrypted or integrity-protected", "Automated KSI: no CIDR overlap between environments", "Automated KSI: every workload has machine identity" presented as FedRAMP 20x Consolidated Rules requirements
findings.problem: No such indicators exist in the CR26 KSI set (AAN_CR26_Reconciliation.md, the corpus's 46-indicator registry; no DNS/CIDR/machine-identity indicator names). These read as invented FedRAMP requirements — the exact thing a hostile reviewer would ask to see an indicator ID for.
findings.fix: Either map each row to a real indicator ID (e.g., KSI-SVC-SNT Securing Network Traffic) or relabel the rows as "architecture capabilities supporting KSI theme X", not "Automated KSI: ...".

findings.claim: KSI-MLA-EVC row: "SD-WAN Manager alert correlation: path quality degradation + flow reroute event = correlated security event"
findings.problem: KSI-MLA-EVC is "Evaluating Configurations" per AAN_CR26_Reconciliation.md (line 43). The file uses it as if EVC meant event correlation; the evidence offered does not attest configuration evaluation.
findings.fix: Move the alert-correlation evidence under KSI-MLA-OSM/LET, or replace the row's evidence with configuration-evaluation evidence (e.g., template compliance evaluation), matching the indicator's actual meaning.

findings.claim: Framework table Standard/Reference cell: "NIST SP 800-37 Rev 2 CA-7"
findings.problem: CA-7 Continuous Monitoring is an SP 800-53 Rev 5 control; SP 800-37 Rev 2 is the RMF process document and contains no control CA-7. Wrong publication attribution.
findings.fix: Cite as "NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-7" (optionally alongside SP 800-37 Rev 2 for the RMF ConMon step).

findings.claim: "Portland to Washington is approximately 4,500 km in a straight line ... 5,400 km fiber ... 27 ms one-way, 54 ms round-trip minimum"
findings.problem: Great-circle Portland, OR to Washington, DC is ~3,750 km, not 4,500 km. The derived fiber distance (~4,500 km with +20%) and propagation floor (~22-23 ms one-way, ~45 ms RTT) inherit a ~20% overstatement. The arithmetic is internally consistent but the base distance is wrong, and this is the book's flagship physics number.
findings.fix: Correct to ~3,750 km straight line, ~4,500 km fiber, ~22.5 ms one-way / ~45 ms RTT. The argument (physics floor >> 5 ms Kerberos expectation) survives unchanged.

findings.claim: §A.3(4): Azure Virtual WAN is "the preferred architecture for agencies already using Azure Government or GCC High"
findings.problem: The appendix scope callout (line ~382) declares "GCC High, DoD IL4/IL5, and FedRAMP High authorizations are out of scope." Recommending a preferred architecture for GCC High agencies inside the same appendix contradicts its own scope statement.
findings.fix: Drop "or GCC High" (keep Azure Government/commercial per the A.3 integration table, which lists Azure commercial + FedRAMP Moderate), or add an explicit out-of-scope pointer.

findings.claim: "The CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model v2.0 Identity pillar at Advanced and Optimal levels requires Certificate-Based Authentication (CBA) as the primary mechanism"
findings.problem: ZTMM v2.0 requires phishing-resistant MFA at those levels; it does not name CBA as the required primary mechanism. Attributing a specific technology mandate to CISA overstates the source (also echoed in the framework table, line ~367).
findings.fix: Soften to "requires phishing-resistant MFA, of which certificate-based authentication is a leading implementation" — or verify the exact ZTMM v2.0 wording before keeping the stronger claim.

findings.claim: "FedRAMP continuous monitoring and OMB M-22-09 expect agencies to operate at Advanced maturity as the production standard" (also "Advanced: ... the FedRAMP ConMon standard posture", line ~296, and the ZTMM table row, line ~352)
findings.problem: Neither FedRAMP ConMon guidance nor M-22-09 designates ZTMM "Advanced" as a standard posture. This is series doctrine (ADR-092 gated-actuation federal ceiling) presented as an external mandate — a hostile ISSO will ask for the citation and there is none.
findings.fix: Attribute the posture to the series' governance doctrine ("this series adopts Advanced/gated actuation as the AO-signable posture") rather than to FedRAMP/OMB.

findings.claim: Appendix A.2/A.3 premise: Microsoft 365 Informed Network Routing (INR) telemetry sharing works with Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN and is "activated" via Cloud OnRamp for SaaS
findings.problem: INR is a Microsoft capability with an enrolled partner list; Cloud OnRamp for SaaS is Cisco-native HTTP probing, not INR telemetry feed. Whether Cisco Catalyst (Viptela) is an INR partner — vs. Meraki or others — is load-bearing for the whole appendix and carries no source link (the authoring spec requires Vendor sources for vendor claims).
findings.fix: Verify Catalyst SD-WAN's INR partner status against Microsoft's published INR partner documentation; either cite it or reframe A.3 as "Cloud OnRamp implements the M365 connectivity principles" without claiming INR activation.

findings.claim: SC-8 row: "IPsec BFD tunnels between all cEdge WAN Edges ... Cisco's DTLS-over-UDP for data-plane encryption; cipher suite is configurable to FIPS 140-3 validated AES-256-GCM"
findings.problem: Per Cisco's own architecture docs, DTLS/TLS secures the control plane (vManage/vSmart connections); the data plane is encrypted with IPsec (ESP), and BFD runs inside the IPsec tunnels — "IPsec BFD tunnels" and "DTLS for data-plane encryption" look garbled. The FIPS 140-3 validation claim needs a CMVP certificate reference. This is the SC-8 satisfaction row — an assessor will read it closely.
findings.fix: Verify against Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN security documentation and reword: IPsec (ESP, AES-256-GCM) for data plane, DTLS/TLS for control plane, BFD inside the tunnels; cite the CMVP cert for the FIPS claim.

findings.claim: Vendor facts with no source links: Microsoft backbone "approximately 200,000 km of dedicated fiber" (~414); Viptela "acquired 2017 and rebranded 2023" (~387); "Microsoft Azure Peering Service (MAPS)" acronym and hand-off behavior (~440)
findings.problem: Not judged true/false — but the series authoring spec (inbox/Federal_AAN_Series_Authoring_Spec.md) requires a Vendor sources: line for vendor claims, and this file has none. These specific figures/names are the kind a reviewer spot-checks.
findings.fix: Add vendor documentation links for each claim or generalize the wording (e.g., "one of the largest private WANs" without the km figure).

findings.claim: Body text: LEO latency "20–40 ms and improving"; fig-02 fig-alt (line ~146): "Starlink LEO for long haul at 20-35ms"
findings.problem: Two different LEO latency ranges within the same book.
findings.fix: Pick one range and use it in both the prose and the figure alt/figure.

findings.claim: "June 11, 2027: No new Rev5 certifications accepted" (and fig-13 alt: "Jun 11 2027 new Rev5 certs cease")
findings.problem: The SSOT event (aan-authority-deadlines.yml, fedramp-rev5-last-applications) is "FedRAMP stops accepting applications for new Rev5 Certifications" — the date is an application cutoff; in-flight applications may still be certified after it. Date matches; the semantics drift.
findings.fix: Reword to "applications for new Rev5 certifications no longer accepted".

findings.claim: "TIC 3.0 Use Cases E (Branch/Remote Office Internet Access) and F (Remote Users)" presented as official CISA names (also line ~290: "Use Cases E and F mandate...")
findings.problem: CISA's TIC 3.0 use cases are named (Branch Office, Remote User), not lettered. Vol I Book 06 (line 308) explicitly declares E/F a series shorthand; Book 05 uses the letters as if official and glosses E with a non-official name, which a reviewer familiar with the CISA documents will flag.
findings.fix: Use the official CISA names with the series-shorthand note Book 06 uses ("Branch Office use case — series shorthand Use Case E").

findings.claim: IA-3 necessity: "No cloud identity provider authenticates a switch port; the enforcement is on the wire, in gear the agency owns" (repeated at line ~241: "no cloud identity provider reaches the switchport"), with ISE OR Mist Access Assurance named as the NAC policy service.
findings.problem: The document's own References table (line ~314) describes Juniper Mist Access Assurance as "Cloud-based NAC / 802.1X." The 802.1X authenticator (switch) is on-prem, but the NAC policy half of the stated closing mechanism ("802.1X authenticator + NAC at the port") is a cloud service in the Juniper realization. Under the book's own Theme F rule (name where the enforcement point sits and the gate follows), a cloud NAC service would need FedRAMP/external-service treatment — yet the IA-3 row assigns only the NIAP/STIG/FIPS/APL gate, and the crossover section covers only the SC-7 SASE case, not the NAC case. A 3PAO would flag the inconsistency.
findings.fix: Narrow the necessity claim to the authenticator function (the switchport enforcement is always customer-owned gear) and explicitly note that a cloud-hosted NAC policy service (e.g., Mist Access Assurance) is the second instance of the gear-becomes-cloud-service crossover, carrying FedRAMP-side evidence for the policy service alongside NIAP evidence for the switch.

findings.claim: Generated table row SC-7(8): mechanism "Forced-proxy egress through the SASE/SWG enforcement point" with accreditation gate "NIAP CC + DISA STIG + FIPS 140-3 + DoDIN APL"; similarly AC-4 (line ~262) names the "NGFW/SASE PEP" under the same all-NIAP gate.
findings.problem: The book's own crossover section (lines ~190-208) states that when the PEP is a cloud-delivered SASE service it passes the FedRAMP gate, not NIAP/STIG/FIPS/APL. Rows whose mechanism text names SASE but whose gate column says NIAP contradict that rule. The table is generated from aan-compliance-spine.yml (gate: niap-stig-fips for these rows), so the contradiction originates in the spine's mechanism wording, not hand-edits — but a reviewer reading only this book sees the gate column contradict the mechanism cell and the crossover doctrine on the same page.
findings.fix: In the spine, reword the SC-7(8)/AC-4 mechanisms for book-net-enforce to the on-prem form this book covers (e.g., "forced-proxy egress at the on-premises NGFW/SWG PEP"), or add a table footnote stating that where the PEP is cloud-delivered SASE the row's gate switches to FedRAMP per the crossover section; then regenerate the table.

findings.claim: DoDIN APL described as "the strictest federal fielding gate," with civilian agencies "frequently" treating APL listing as an assurance signal.
findings.problem: Both the superlative ("strictest") and the frequency claim ("frequently") are unsupported comparatives with no source; neither is verifiable against an SSOT and an assessor could challenge either.
findings.fix: Soften to a descriptive statement (e.g., "the fielding gate for connection to DoD networks; some civilian agencies treat APL listing as an additional assurance signal") or cite a source.

findings.claim: Vendor-realization matrix and references: product identities and capabilities (Catalyst SD-WAN/Viptela, Prisma SD-WAN, Session Smart Router/128T, ISE+TrustSec, Mist Access Assurance, Apstra, Cortex XDR/XSIAM, GlobalProtect, Secure Client/AnyConnect), the implicit premise that each hardware product line is NIAP-evaluated/CMVP-validated/APL-listed, and the FedRAMP authorization status of Prisma Access and Cisco Secure Access.
findings.problem: These are external vendor/registry facts not verifiable against in-repo SSOTs. The document hedges correctly ("candidate implementation, not a recommendation"; validation "against the current NIAP PCL, CMVP list, DISA STIG, and DoDIN APL at time of buy"; SASE status "verified on the FedRAMP Marketplace at procurement") — flagging per category, not judging true/false.
findings.fix: No text change required; at procurement or formal review, verify each cell against the NIAP PCL, CMVP list, DoDIN APL, and FedRAMP Marketplace as the document itself instructs.

findings.claim: "Under TIC 3.0, a branch running Direct Internet Access is permissible *only when* the security-capabilities catalog is satisfied at a distributed enforcement point."
findings.problem: This states an absolute permissibility condition attributed to CISA TIC 3.0 guidance. TIC 3.0 is risk-based use-case guidance; whether the Branch Office use case makes catalog satisfaction a strict precondition (vs. applying relevant capabilities per agency risk tolerance) is an external-document characterization not verifiable against in-repo SSOTs.
findings.fix: Soften to track the guidance's own framing (e.g., "DIA at a branch is exercised under the TIC 3.0 Branch Office use case, which requires the relevant security capabilities to be applied at a distributed enforcement point") or verify the exact conditional language against the CISA TIC 3.0 Branch Office Use Case document.

findings.claim: NIST table row reads "SI-3 | Malware Protection"; line 271 also says "SI-3 (malware protection via SSL inspection)".
findings.problem: The official SP 800-53r5 title of SI-3 is "Malicious Code Protection" (reference/nist-800-53r5-controls.json, catalog v5.2.0; the spine registry uses the same title at aan-compliance-spine.yml line 292). Every other row in this table uses the exact official title, so the table reads as a titles column and SI-3's is factually wrong.
findings.fix: Change "Malware Protection" to "Malicious Code Protection" in the line-289 table row (the fig-05 alt text and line 271 prose can keep lowercase descriptive wording, but the table must match the catalog).

findings.claim: "Federated authentication events (IA-8): Entra ID → Amazon Connect SAML assertions must produce KSI-verifiable authentication telemetry."
findings.problem: IA-8 is "Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users)" per the SSOT catalog. The users described are agency agents authenticating via the agency IdP — organizational users, covered by IA-2. IA-8 fits only if the claim is explicitly framed from AWS's (the CSP's) boundary perspective, which the text does not do; as written, a 3PAO would flag the mapping.
findings.fix: Cite IA-2 (or IA-2/IA-8 with an explicit note that IA-8 applies from the CSP-boundary perspective) for agent federation telemetry.

findings.claim: Two callouts are titled "Closure Necessity — SC-8 on the voice path" and "Closure Necessity — SC-7 / SC-7(7) on distributed egress", and line 271 states the SD-WAN overlay "closes SC-8 and SI-4" and the SASE SSE stack "closes AC-4, SC-7, SI-3, AU-2/AU-12, CA-7".
findings.problem: The spine registry (aan-compliance-spine.yml) records ZERO closure rows for book-06. SC-8's closure (necessity: true) and SC-7/AC-4/SI-4 closures are registered to book-net-enforce with different mechanisms; AU-12/CA-7 to book-evidence-fabric. SC-7 is registered necessity: false, and no SC-7(7) row exists at all — so Book 06 declares a Closure-Necessity anchor the registry does not recognize. "Closure Necessity" is a defined spine term (necessity: true, no alternate path); using it for unregistered controls contradicts the SSOT.
findings.fix: Either register book-06 closure/necessity rows in the spine (or re-attribute the SC-7(7) necessity argument), or rephrase the callouts and line 271 to say the components 'provide the mechanism for' controls whose closure is owned by Book 07 (net-enforce) and the evidence-fabric book, with cross-references.

findings.claim: Line 271: "The SD-WAN overlay closes ... SI-4" and "The SASE SSE stack closes ... AU-2/AU-12"; the NIST table (lines 290–291) attributes SI-4 to "AAN — application-layer telemetry, behavioral analysis" and AU-12 to "AAN logging"; fig-05 alt puts SI-4/AU-12 on the analytics/logging side, not SD-WAN/SASE.
findings.problem: The same file gives three different owners for SI-4 and AU-12 (SD-WAN, SASE SSE, AAN). A reviewer tracing which mechanism actually generates SI-4/AU-12 evidence cannot reconcile the three statements.
findings.fix: Pick one mechanism per control and use it consistently in line 271, the table, and the figure alt text.

findings.claim: Exec summary point 3 (and fig-15 alt, line 189): Teams Phone "introduces no new boundary complications."
findings.problem: The document itself contradicts this at line 368: the PSTN interconnect "is a boundary crossing by definition," the SBC "must be documented in the SSP as a boundary interface," and a cloud SBC must independently hold FedRAMP Moderate+ authorization (line 201). Those are new boundary obligations. A hostile ISSO would quote the two passages against each other.
findings.fix: Soften to "introduces no new authorization boundary beyond the existing GCC Moderate ATO; the PSTN/SBC interconnect is the one new boundary interface and is documented in this book."

findings.claim: Body text: Portland-via-MPLS one-way network latency "80–110 ms"; figure alt texts (lines 64 and 140): "Portland MPLS at 100-130ms."
findings.problem: The body and two figures give different latency ranges for the same path. Neither is reproducible from the stated derivation (~50 ms propagation + inspection/queuing overhead does not pin either range), and the mismatch suggests the figures were drawn from a superseded estimate.
findings.fix: Align body and figures on one range, and keep the existing "engineering estimate — validate with per-site measurement" caveat attached to it.

findings.claim: Delay-budget arithmetic: line 70 says jitter buffer is "typically 50–80 ms adaptive" leaving "approximately 50–80 ms" of network budget; the WebRTC table and the rest of the doc use a flat "75 ms network budget"; fig-10 alt shows a "75ms budget gauge" containing 20 ms codec + 30 ms jitter buffer + 25 ms remaining; fig-01 alt uses a 50 ms jitter buffer.
findings.problem: Three different jitter-buffer values (50–80 / 50 / 30 ms) and two incompatible budget models: the text defines 75 ms as what remains AFTER codec and jitter buffer are subtracted from 150 ms, while fig-10 double-counts by putting codec and jitter buffer INSIDE the 75 ms, implying only 25 ms of network allowance. The pass/fail threshold this book is built on cannot be reproduced consistently from its own numbers.
findings.fix: Fix one decomposition (e.g., 150 = 20 codec + 55 jitter buffer + 75 network) and propagate it to line 70, the WebRTC table, and both figure alts.

findings.claim: Federal Framework table cites "OMB M-22-09 §4" as the mandate for per-DSCP steering (DSCP EF), and "TIC 3.0; OMB M-22-09" / "CISA ZTMM v2.0 Networks pillar" for active-active multipath with sub-second failover.
findings.problem: These mandate attributions are not in any in-repo SSOT and cannot be verified here.
