findings.fix: Per the series authoring spec (inbox/Federal_AAN_Series_Authoring_Spec.md), add Vendor sources: links where vendor accreditation status is asserted, or soften to "accredited through the NIAP / DISA STIG / FIPS 140-3 / DoDIN APL gate (Theme F; verify listings per model at deployment)".

findings.claim: "Ten of the twenty-nine CR26 KSIs are attestable by ScuBA-class tooling alone" (also line 121 "all 29 CR26 KSIs", line 340 "all 29 FedRAMP 20x CR26 KSIs", and the fig-alt at line 79).
findings.problem: The 29 are the series' INTERNAL rule ids (KSI-001..029 in src/uiao/ksi/rules/). The repo's own CR26 catalog spec (src/uiao/canon/specs/fedramp-cr26-ksi-mapping.md, lines 81-82) records the actual CR26 KSI schema as 10 themes / 46 KSI controls. Calling the internal 29 "CR26 KSIs" in body text asserts a CR26 count that is factually wrong; a 3PAO comparing against the FedRAMP CR26 indicator list would reject it. The closing footer (line 365-367) correctly discloses "internal KSI decomposition (modeled on the FedRAMP 20x CR26 KSI schema)" — the body contradicts its own footer.
findings.fix: Everywhere "29 CR26 KSIs" appears (lines 49, 121, 340, fig-alt line 79), rephrase to "the twenty-nine KSI rules of the series' internal decomposition (KSI-001..029, modeled on the CR26 KSI schema)" or similar; reserve "CR26 KSI" for the actual KSI-XXX-YYY indicators (46 per the CR26 catalog spec).

findings.claim: Module A1 lists "IA-2 (+enhancements 1, 2, 11)" among the controls slot 1 closes.
findings.problem: IA-2(11) is WITHDRAWN in NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (incorporated into IA-2(6) "Access to Accounts — Separate Device"). The in-repo catalog JSON deliberately includes withdrawn ids (see its _provenance note: "a withdrawn control cited as live is a title/semantics question"), so the id resolving to "Remote Access — Separate Device" does not make it a live Rev 5 closure target — that is the Rev 4 title retained on the withdrawn entry. A Rev 5 curriculum teaching assessors to trace closures to a withdrawn enhancement is exactly what a hostile 3PAO flags. The same stale citation exists upstream in src/uiao/adapters/fedramp_aan_catalog/mappings/slot-01-identity-evidence.yaml (lines 35 and 83), which is likely the source.
findings.fix: Replace enhancement 11 with the live Rev 5 equivalent (IA-2(6), or the Moderate-baseline set IA-2(8)/(12) as appropriate) here AND in slot-01-identity-evidence.yaml so the curriculum and the adapter stay in lockstep.

findings.claim: Module A0: "20x mandatory for new authorizations January 2027".
findings.problem: The SSOT (aan-authority-deadlines.yml, id cr26-mandatory, 2027-01-01) says CR26 becomes mandatory and EXISTING Rev5 Certifications must adopt — and a separate entry (fedramp-rev5-last-applications) says FedRAMP keeps accepting applications for NEW Rev5 Certifications until 2027-06-11. So "mandatory for new authorizations" in January 2027 contradicts the registry: a new authorization can still enter via Rev5 until June 2027. The date matches; the characterization does not.
findings.fix: Restate as "CR26 mandatory January 1, 2027 (existing Rev5 Certifications must adopt; new Rev5 applications accepted until June 11, 2027)" or simply "CR26 mandatory January 2027".

findings.claim: Module A2 titles slot 2 the "Addressing Control Plane" (and the line-330 table row "2 — Addressing").
findings.problem: The book/closure-registry SSOT (aan-compliance-spine.yml, slots block, line ~232) names slot-02 "Data" (slot-02-data) and binds data-flow closures to it (e.g. AC-4 and SI-12 for book-sn-saas → slot-02-data). The adapter mappings instead have slot-02-addressing-evidence.yaml (slot: addressing). The track matches the adapter but contradicts the spine — the two registries this book claims "cannot silently drift" (line 83) have in fact drifted on slot 2's identity, and the track has no Data slot at all (Purview lands in slot 4).
findings.fix: Reconcile the slot-02 name between aan-compliance-spine.yml and the fedramp_aan_catalog mappings (pick Addressing or Data as canonical), then align this module's title and the reference table; at minimum add a note acknowledging the spine's slot-02-data naming.

findings.claim: Reference table column "Tool-attestable alone?": slot 1 = No, slot 3 = No, slot 4 = Partial, slot 6 = Partial.
findings.problem: The No/Partial assignments cannot be reproduced from the adapter mappings. Slot 1's mapping binds four of the ten ScuBA-attestable rules (KSI-001, KSI-002, KSI-003, KSI-009) and slot 3's binds KSI-004, yet both are marked "No", while slot 4 is "Partial" on the identical basis (KSI-005, KSI-010 bound there). No stated rule explains why ScuBA-rule presence makes slot 4 Partial but leaves slots 1 and 3 No — an assessor cross-checking the mappings the book says to run will hit this immediately.
findings.fix: Either mark slots 1 and 3 "Partial" for consistency, or state the derivation rule for the column (e.g. "Partial only where ScuBA config exports substitute for a share of the slot's own evidence") so the values are reproducible.

findings.claim: Module A6: "the BOD 26-04 submission (December 7, 2026)" and checkpoint "state the BOD 26-04 submission story — which SBOM artifacts Vol IV Book 02 requires".
findings.problem: The SSOT event for 2026-12-07 (id bod-26-04-vdr-ver) is "remediation timelines in force; FedRAMP VDR/VER mandatory adoption" — a compliance-in-force date, not a one-time "submission" deadline. Additionally, BOD 26-04 per the registry concerns VDR/VER and risk-based remediation; SBOM artifacts come from the series' own SCRM evidence contract, not from a BOD 26-04 submission requirement. Framing Dec 7 as "the BOD 26-04 submission" of SBOMs conflates the directive with the series' internal artifact chain.
findings.fix: Rephrase to "the BOD 26-04 VDR/VER in-force date (December 7, 2026)" (matching Module A0's correct phrasing at line 112) and attribute the SBOM artifacts to the Vol IV Book 02 evidence contract rather than to BOD 26-04.

findings.claim: Module A7 controls: "CP-2 (+3 enhancements), CP-3, CP-4 (+2), CP-6, CP-7 (+3), CP-8 (+2)".
findings.problem: "CP-4 (+2)" fails both readings. Read as a count, the feeding sources carry ONE CP-4 enhancement: Vol IV Book 01 cites only CP-4(1), and slot-07-continuity-evidence.yaml closes only CP-4/CP-4(1). Read as the enhancement number, CP-4(2) "Alternate Processing Site" appears in neither the book nor the mapping — and it is a High-baseline enhancement, out of the series' Moderate-only scope. (CP-2 +3, CP-7 +3, CP-8 +2 do reproduce as counts against the slot-07 mapping; CP-6 is shown with no count though the mapping carries CP-6(1)/(3) — the notation is inconsistent.)
findings.fix: Change to "CP-4 (+1)" (i.e. CP-4(1)) and normalize the enhancement notation across the list (either counts everywhere, including CP-6 (+2), or explicit enhancement numbers everywhere).

findings.claim: Module A0: "Class A window opened August 2026".
findings.problem: Past tense for a future event: the SSOT (fedramp-20x-class-a) dates the Class A pipeline opening to 2026-08-03, after this document's Date Code (2026-07-09) and after today (2026-07-14). The month is correct; "opened" is not yet true and will read as a factual error to anyone checking the timeline before August.
findings.fix: Change to "Class A pipeline opens August 3, 2026" (future/neutral tense), which also matches the deadline gate's keyword pattern "Class A (pipeline )?opens".

findings.claim: The KSI Closure Necessity Matrix 'must reconcile with Vol 0 Book 00 and Vol IV Book 06: 10 attestable by tooling alone, 19 architecture-bound, 29 total' — presented as the certification exam's answer key.
findings.problem: It reconciles only at the bottom-line totals. Vol 0 Book 00's authoritative matrix (Vol_0_Book_00_FedAAN_Executive_Summary.qmd lines 661-670) decomposes the 19 as: KSI-011..016 SCR/slot-06 (Vol IV Bks 02-03), KSI-017..021 PIY = privacy program + PII data-flow maps/slot-05 (Vol IV Bk 04), KSI-022 CED-RAT/slot-08, KSI-023..029 CED/INR/RPL/slots 04+07. Book 03's matrix contradicts this row-by-row: it defines KSI-PIY as 'Authoritative IPAM/DDI + device identity' homed at Vol I Bk 01/02 · Vol III Bk 03/04 (Book 00 says PIY = privacy, homed at Vol IV Bk 04); it carries architecture-bound rows for KSI-IAM and KSI-CNA, families that per Book 00 have ZERO rules outside the ScuBA 10 ('the IAM/CNA/SVC/MLA themes... the 10 ScuBA baseline rules attest'); and it labels slot-4 rules KSI-MLA and slot-6 rules KSI-CMT where Book 00 assigns INR and SCR. A candidate reconstructing the matrix from Book 00 — exactly what the exam demands — produces a different table. A hostile 3PAO running the invited reconciliation would reject the 'must reconcile' claim.
findings.fix: Either restructure the matrix to Book 00's per-rule decomposition (SCR 6 / PIY-privacy 5 / CED 1 / CED-INR-RPL 7 + ScuBA 10), or narrow the reconciliation claim to the 10/19/29 totals and state explicitly that the family/slot framing here follows Vol V Book 01's training-module model, not Book 00's rule-ID decomposition.

findings.claim: 'One row per active KSI rule' with a pre-computed bottom line of 10 tool-attestable / 19 architecture-bound / 29 total (prose line 174-179, caption line 192).
findings.problem: The printed table is one row per KSI FAMILY (9 rows for 29 rules), and its 'Rules' column contains words ('identity', 'inventory', 'network'...) instead of rule counts for every row except the ScuBA row. The 19 cannot be reproduced from the table as printed — the reader must leave the document to verify the split the caption asserts. Book 00's version of the same table carries per-row counts (e.g. 'KSI-011..014 (4)', 'KSI-022 (1)') that sum to 29; this one does not.
findings.fix: Put per-row rule counts in the 'Rules' column so the rows sum to 29, and change the prose from 'one row per active KSI rule' to 'one row per rule family' (or expand to a true per-rule table).

findings.claim: Matrix row KSI-PIY: slots '2, 5', series home 'Vol I Bk 01/02 · Vol III Bk 03/04'.
findings.problem: The same file's Slot 5 rubric (line 122) lists the slot-5 feeding books as 'Vol I Bk 02 · Vol III Bk 01/03/04 · Vol IV Bk 04', and Vol V Book 01's slot table (line 333) agrees. The matrix — declared 'the authoritative artifact of the Academy' — silently drops Vol III Bk 01 and Vol IV Bk 04 from the union of slots 2 and 5. A candidate scoring against the rubric and checking against the matrix gets two different book lists for the same KSI family.
findings.fix: Make the KSI-PIY series-home cell the union of the slot-2 and slot-5 rubric book lists: Vol I Bk 01/02 · Vol III Bk 01/03/04 · Vol IV Bk 04 (or footnote why Bk 01/IV-04 are rubric-only).

findings.claim: Slot 7 level-2 evidence: 'CP-2 through CP-10 with enhancement counts right'.
findings.problem: The range sweeps in CP-5 ('Contingency Plan Update'), which is withdrawn in 800-53 Rev 5 (incorporated into CP-2) — there are no CP-5 enhancement counts to get 'right'. It also contradicts the mapping the rubric claims to mirror: Vol V Book 01 Module A7 lists CP-2(+3), CP-3, CP-4(+2), CP-6, CP-7(+3), CP-8(+2) — no CP-5, and CP-9/CP-10 appear only in Vol IV Bk 01 itself, not in the module's control list. An exam criterion that requires enumerating a withdrawn control is exactly what the file's own common check ('no invented controls') forbids.
findings.fix: Replace the range with the explicit list from Vol V Book 01 Module A7 (CP-2, CP-3, CP-4, CP-6, CP-7, CP-8, plus CP-9/CP-10 if the Vol IV Bk 01 closure set is intended), or write 'the CP family Vol IV Bk 01 closes (CP-5 withdrawn in Rev 5)'.

findings.claim: Slot 2 is named 'Addressing (KSI-PIY)' with IPAM inventory evidence 'referenced from the slot-02 mapping' (lines 94-100, scoring sheet '2 — addressing' line 229).
findings.problem: The compliance spine's slot registry (aan-compliance-spine.yml line 232) defines slot-02-data as 'Data', and Vol 0 Book 00 uses it the same way ('the data and telemetry slots (slot-02, slot-04) on Vol III Books 01, 02, and 05'); spine closures bound to slot-02-data are data-lineage controls (AC-4/SI-12), not IPAM inventory. The Vol V training track's slot 2 = Addressing/IPAM contradicts the spine SSOT's slot 2 = Data. Inherited from Vol V Book 01 (Module A2), but this book repeats and grades it, so an assessor reconciling the rubric's 'slot-02 mapping' against the spine finds no addressing slot.
findings.fix: Align the training track's slot names with the spine slots block (or add an explicit note that Vol V module numbering diverges from the spine's evidence-slot registry and give the translation), coordinating the same fix in Vol V Book 01.

findings.claim: SailPoint Identity University row maps to 'Vol I Bk 04' with note 'Joiner-mover-leaver governance for the HRIT lifecycle; documented NERM boundary exception'.
findings.problem: Vol I Book 04 (HRIT Identity & Org SSOT) contains no mention of SailPoint or NERM. The series documents SailPoint ISC and the 'SailPoint NERM ... (series carve-out)' in Vol III Book 01 (Privileged Access Management, ~lines 988-995). A reviewer following the 'documented' pointer to the cited volume finds nothing.
findings.fix: Add Vol III Bk 01 to the Volumes column (or replace Vol I Bk 04), or reword the note so 'documented' points at the book that actually documents the NERM carve-out.

findings.claim: Lab coverage is complete: the setups table covers modules B1, B2, B5, B6, and 'Modules B3 ..., B7 ..., and B8 ... intentionally have no tenant lab'.
findings.problem: Vol V Book 02 defines eight modules B1-B8. Module B4 (Data Platform Modernization, Vol II Books 01-03) appears in neither the lab setups table nor the intentionally-no-lab list, so its lab status is silently unaccounted for — even though the book carries a Data Platform training section and claims each Track B module ends with labs whose environments 'the environments below stand up'.
findings.fix: Either add a B4 lab row (e.g., SQL Server in containers / Azure SQL trial, Tier F or T) or add B4 to the intentionally-no-tenant-lab paragraph with a rationale.

findings.claim: Zscaler row asserts a 'separate Government Academy for federal' as a factual note.
findings.problem: The Research Queue (line ~230) lists 'Zscaler Government Academy' as a candidate 'identified but not yet verified', while the Identity & Zero Trust table already asserts its existence as fact. Internal tension between an asserted row and the book's own not-yet-verified queue; the external offering itself needs verification (not judged here).
findings.fix: Either verify and cite the Government Academy (removing it from the research queue) or soften the table note to match the queue's unverified status.

findings.claim: Tier T requires 'a Microsoft 365 developer/trial tenant + Azure trial', and Cost Notes state 'M365 E5 developer/trial tenants cover Entra ID P2 (PIM), Purview, and Defender features for the trial window'.
findings.problem: This is load-bearing for lab feasibility (four of five labs are Tier T). Microsoft has materially changed Developer Program sandbox-tenant availability and trial-tenant feature entitlements over time; whether a free developer/trial tenant currently exists for the target audience and includes Entra ID P2, Purview, and Defender needs external verification against Microsoft (not judged true/false here).
findings.fix: Verify current M365 developer/trial tenant availability and E5 feature coverage against Microsoft documentation and cite it, or note the acquisition path (e.g., CDX/partner tenant) explicitly.

findings.claim: 'Sentinel bills per GB ingested — the lab keeps ingestion in the free-tier range by using a single VM/forwarder and seeded events.'
findings.problem: 'Free-tier range' implies a specific Sentinel/Log Analytics free allowance (historically a 31-day/10 GB-per-day trial plus limited free data sources); whether a low-ingestion lab is actually free depends on current Azure pricing terms that need external verification.
findings.fix: Name the specific free mechanism relied on (Sentinel free trial window, free data connectors) with a citation, or reword to 'minimal cost'.

findings.claim: AWS Skill Builder row maps to 'Vol I Bk 05, 06' as 'Amazon Connect training for the N8NN contact-center boundary exception'.
findings.problem: The N8NN contact-center exception appears only in Vol I Book 06 (Federal Telecommunications Modernization) and Book 00; Vol I Book 05 (Network Modernization) mentions neither N8NN nor Amazon Connect, so the Bk 05 mapping is unsupported.
findings.fix: Drop 'Bk 05' from the Volumes column or add a rationale tying Amazon Connect training to Book 05 content.

findings.claim: Cisco rows map to Vol I Bk 02/05/06 and Palo Alto to Vol I Bk 05/06; only the Juniper row maps to Vol I Bk 07.
findings.problem: The spine registers Vol I Book 07 as 'Network Enforcement Substrate (Cisco/Palo Alto/Juniper)' — a book explicitly named for all three vendors — yet the training catalog points only Juniper's row at it. A reviewer using the catalog to staff the Book 07 build would miss the Cisco and Palo Alto training rows.
findings.fix: Add Vol I Bk 07 to the Cisco (Cisco U.) and Palo Alto Networks volume mappings.

findings.claim: Routine vendor-catalog facts asserted across the tables: exam codes and successor claims (SC-401 'successor to SC-400', AZ-700, DP-300, SC-100), 'CISA Learning (successor to FedVTE)', Fortinet 'Free NSE-track courses', Qualys 'Free certified courses with labs', Infoblox 'free Launchpad', Linux Foundation course codes LFEL1007/LFD121, Netskope 'Netskope One administrator/professional' names.
findings.problem: These are external vendor/portal facts that change without notice (Fortinet in particular rebranded NSE-track certifications); the link-check CI catches dead URLs but not renamed programs, retired exams, or pricing changes. Not judged true/false here — flagged as the standing external-verification surface of this catalog.
findings.fix: Rely on the existing verify-at-procurement disclaimer, and add a last-verified date column (or per-row date) so staleness of vendor program names is visible, mirroring the aan-authority-deadlines.yml pattern.

findings.claim: "Federal control closure is operated at the GCC-Moderate ServiceNow front door (Chapter 7)"
findings.problem: aan-compliance-spine.yml registers Vol VIII closures under TWO books: book-ddi-servicenow (Chapter 7: CM-3, CM-5, AU-2) AND book-ddi-xplat (Chapter 6: SC-20, SC-22, CM-8 — the naming-plane closures, whose mechanism is the authoritative Infoblox DDI plane, not the ServiceNow front door). The intro presents Chapter 7 as the sole locus of federal control closure, which contradicts the spine registry a reviewer would check first.
findings.fix: Amend the scope note to say control closure is registered at Chapter 6 (naming-plane controls SC-20/SC-22/CM-8) and Chapter 7 (change-governance controls CM-3/CM-5/AU-2), or say the ServiceNow front door operates the change-governance closures specifically.

findings.claim: "This is assembly of certified products — ServiceNow's CPG Terraform Connector and the Service Graph Connector for Infoblox — not custom glue."
findings.problem: The certification status of both connectors is a ServiceNow Store / vendor-listing claim that cannot be verified from any in-repo SSOT (not judged true or false here). It is load-bearing: it underwrites the "not custom glue" assurance. It also sits in tension with the same paragraph pointing to servicenow-app/ (Script Includes, REST Message, Flow blueprint, MID gate), which IS custom-built content a 3PAO would classify as custom glue.
findings.fix: Add vendor-source links for both connectors' certification/listing status per the series' vendor-claims convention, and soften "not custom glue" to acknowledge the importable scoped app is custom scaffolding around certified connectors.

findings.claim: Comparison table row: "Air-gapped / gov cloud | Fully self-contained | Requires outbound 443 to Portal"
findings.problem: For a federal audience this row is load-bearing (it steers gov-cloud readers to NIOS Grid and flags Universal DDI as boundary-crossing). Whether a NIOS Grid is "fully self-contained" in air-gapped/gov-cloud deployments (licensing activation, threat-feed updates, support telemetry) is a vendor claim; the chapter's sources list only Infoblox product marketing pages, which do not establish it. Not judged true or false — needs vendor-doc verification.
findings.fix: Cite a specific Infoblox deployment/air-gap doc for the self-contained claim, or qualify the cell (e.g. "self-contained control plane; licensing/feed updates handled offline per vendor doc").

findings.claim: "...then the cross-platform operations appendix, before touching a single deployment."
findings.problem: Cross-Platform Operations & Multi-Cloud Governance is Chapter 6 (spine slot VIII-06, source infoblox-ddi-book/06-cross-platform-operations.md), a registered book — not an appendix. The volume has a distinct Appendix A (VIII-A, sizing/cost/IPv6/DHCP), so calling Chapter 6 an appendix misdirects the reader and mislabels a spine-registered book.
findings.fix: Change to "the cross-platform operations chapter (Chapter 6)" and optionally mention Appendix A separately.

findings.claim: Native-DDI baseline table (0.1): "no native IPAM (Azure IPAM is a sample app)", "VPC IPAM", "no first-class IPAM" (GCP), "no native IPAM" (OCI), "no native enterprise IPAM" (VMware/NSX-T); and 0.3: "Universal DDI (formerly BloxOne DDI)"
findings.problem: These per-CSP product-capability characterizations and the product-rename claim are external vendor/platform facts not verifiable from any in-repo SSOT (not judged true or false). The chapter's sources cover landing-zone docs and Infoblox product pages generally, but no source is tied to the specific IPAM-capability assertions the table makes.
findings.fix: Anchor each table row's capability claim to the specific CSP doc (e.g. the Azure IPAM sample-app repo, AWS VPC IPAM docs) in the sources list, matching the series' vendor-sources convention.

findings.claim: Prerequisites table states as fact: 'Esv3-series (NIOS < 9.0.6); Esv5-series supported from NIOS 9.0.5+'
findings.problem: Section 9 (line ~214-217) directly undercuts this precision: 'Model-specific vCPU/RAM and the exact Esv5 minimum version are release-dependent — confirm against the NIOS version's supported-appliance list.' A reviewer will ask which statement is authoritative; the specific 9.0.5/9.0.6 cutoffs are vendor version claims not verifiable from any in-repo SSOT, and the two thresholds overlap oddly (9.0.5 apparently supports both series while Esv3 dies at 9.0.6).
findings.fix: Either hedge the section 4 table the same way section 9 does ("version-dependent — see Infoblox supported-appliance list") or pin both thresholds to the specific Infoblox supported-appliances page already in Sources and make sections 4 and 9 consistent.

findings.claim: vNIOS Marketplace offer 'infoblox.infoblox_nios_on_azure' is deployable on 'Azure public and Azure Government clouds only' (repeated in section 10 as the sovereignty/Gov-cloud guidance)
findings.problem: This availability claim is load-bearing for the section 10 'Sovereignty / Gov cloud' recommendation, but Marketplace availability by cloud (and the listing ID itself) is an external vendor/marketplace fact that changes over time and cannot be verified from any in-repo SSOT. Not judged true or false — flagging for external verification per policy.
findings.fix: Verify the listing ID and Azure Government availability against the Azure Marketplace / Infoblox docs already cited in Sources, and date-stamp the verification.

findings.claim: 'A forwarding ruleset holds up to 1,000 rules ... ample for a large privatelink footprint'
findings.problem: Microsoft service limit quoted as a hard number and used to support the 'ample' conclusion; Azure DNS Private Resolver limits are external facts subject to change and not verifiable in-repo. Not judged true or false.
findings.fix: Verify against the cited Microsoft Private Resolver endpoints-and-rulesets doc and note the verification date, or soften to 'the ruleset rule limit (see Microsoft docs) comfortably covers a large privatelink footprint'.

findings.claim: Grid transport specifics — 1194/udp Grid VPN tunnel, 2114/tcp 'Grid CRAM auth (precedes VPN)' — and Universal DDI SaaS endpoints 'csp.infoblox.com / csp.eu.infoblox.com' on outbound 443
findings.problem: Port/protocol semantics and SaaS endpoint hostnames are Infoblox product facts that a 3PAO would trace to current vendor documentation before accepting them in an NSG/boundary design; they cannot be confirmed from any in-repo SSOT. Not judged true or false — the Sources section does cite the relevant Infoblox ports page.
findings.fix: Confirm ports and CSP hostnames against the cited Infoblox 'Source and Destination Ports for Services' and 'NIOS-X Connectivity' pages and record the verification date.

findings.claim: Version-gated Infoblox feature claims: NIOS 9.0.5+ supports M7i/R7i shapes and ships in-built licenses from Marketplace; NIOS 9.0.4+ single vDiscovery job spans multiple AWS Organization accounts across regions including GovCloud; Route 53 integration supported on GovCloud from NIOS 8.6.3.
findings.problem: These specific version thresholds are load-bearing for sizing and GovCloud deployment decisions but cannot be verified against any in-repo SSOT; if a threshold is off by a point release, a GovCloud deployment plan built on this chapter fails. Sources are cited (Infoblox NAIG docs) but not pinned to a doc version/date.
findings.fix: Verify each version threshold against the current Infoblox NIOS for AWS install guide and release notes; add the doc revision/date checked next to each version claim or in the Sources entries.

findings.claim: The 2025 Amazon VPC IPAM ↔ Infoblox integration lets you designate Infoblox as the management authority for a VPC IPAM private scope, pull CIDRs via BYOIP from Infoblox Universal IPAM into the top-level AWS IPAM pool, and applies to private scopes only.
findings.problem: This is a very recent (Nov 2025) AWS feature whose exact mechanics (authority designation, BYOIP flow, private-scope-only restriction) are asserted in detail; a 3PAO would ask for confirmation against current AWS documentation since early-release feature semantics change. Cannot be validated from in-repo SSOTs.
findings.fix: Re-verify the integration mechanics and the private-scope-only restriction against the linked AWS VPC IPAM documentation before publication; note the verification date.

findings.claim: Grid communication port specifics: VPN tunnel on 1194/udp, Grid control channel on 2114/tcp (with a caveat that some guides list 2114/udp), and Infoblox AWS API proxy on 8787/tcp egress.
findings.problem: Security-group port numbers are copied into deployable SGs (aws-lz-automation/terraform/securitygroups.tf); wrong ports break Grid join silently. The 2114 tcp-vs-udp hedge acknowledges vendor-doc ambiguity but the table cannot be confirmed from in-repo SSOTs.
findings.fix: Confirm the port/protocol set against the current Infoblox NIOS appliance port-usage documentation and align the chapter table with securitygroups.tf; drop or resolve the 2114/udp hedge once confirmed.

findings.claim: A Route 53 Resolver 'delegation inbound endpoint' can delegate a private-hosted-zone subdomain to the Route 53 VPC resolver.
findings.problem: Delegation-type inbound endpoints are a recent Route 53 Resolver feature; the delegation direction described (Infoblox-side subdomain delegated to the VPC resolver) needs confirmation against current AWS docs, as the feature is documented as delegating subdomains from external DNS into Route 53 via the endpoint.
findings.fix: Verify the delegation endpoint semantics against the AWS Route 53 Resolver documentation and adjust the sentence to match the documented direction of delegation.

findings.claim: DNS Armor (Google Cloud) is 'GA since Jan 2026' (repeated at line 226 as 'GA Jan 2026').
findings.problem: A specific general-availability date for a third-party Google/Infoblox product is asserted as fact twice; it cannot be verified against any in-repo SSOT and a 3PAO would ask for the announcement citation pinned to that date. The Sources section links the Infoblox partner page and press release but neither is quoted with a date.
findings.fix: Verify the DNS Armor GA date against the Google Cloud or Infoblox announcement and either cite it inline (e.g., footnote to the specific release note) or soften to 'generally available' without a month if the date cannot be pinned.

findings.claim: Marketplace listing names: 'Infoblox vNIOS for Google Cloud' (line 57) and 'Infoblox Universal DDI for Google's Cloud WAN' (line 58) are stated as the exact Google Cloud Marketplace listings.
findings.problem: Exact Marketplace SKU/listing names change; these are external-catalog facts not verifiable in-repo. If a listing name drifts, the step-by-step deployment instruction at line 87-88 ('From Google Cloud Marketplace launch Infoblox vNIOS for Google Cloud') breaks.
findings.fix: Re-verify both listing titles against the current Google Cloud Marketplace before publication, or hedge with 'the current Infoblox vNIOS Marketplace listing' and rely on the Sources links for the canonical name.

findings.claim: "There is no VMware Marketplace SKU that auto-deploys the Grid" and the Aria plug-in "carries no separate per-VM license beyond the underlying Grid"; licensing is "by appliance model/subscription".
findings.problem: These are negative marketplace-availability and licensing/procurement claims about Infoblox and the VMware/Broadcom Marketplace with no direct citation in the Sources list (the cited docs cover deployment and the plug-in, not the absence of a marketplace SKU or the license terms). Marketplace listings and licensing terms change; a reviewer relying on this for procurement could be misled if stale.
findings.fix: Either add a dated vendor source supporting the marketplace/licensing statements or hedge them ("as of this writing, Infoblox does not publish a Marketplace SKU that...") and mark for periodic re-verification.

findings.claim: Support matrix: Aria Automation / vRA 8.9.1 or later, Infoblox IPAM plug-in 1.5+, Grid WAPI v2.7+ (restated at line ~196 as "vRA/Aria 8.9.1+, plug-in 1.5+, WAPI v2.7").
findings.problem: Specific vendor version-compatibility thresholds sourced from Infoblox/Broadcom docs (cited) but version-dependent and not independently verifiable in-repo; unlike the sizing table (line 229) this matrix carries no "confirm against the current guide" hedge.
findings.fix: Extend the version-dependency hedge already used for the sizing table to the Aria/plug-in/WAPI support matrix, or pin the claim to the specific plug-in doc version cited.

findings.claim: "so no address is used in OCI that IPAM doesn't already know about"
findings.problem: Absolute claim with no enforcing mechanism. Pre-provision allocation via Terraform only covers pipeline-provisioned resources; anyone attaching a VNIC via the OCI console, or OCI platform DHCP handing out addresses inside a VCN, uses addresses IPAM has not pre-allocated. The chapter itself concedes this in Day-2 operations (line ~294: reconcile drift for 'CIDRs added in OCI outside pipelines'), which contradicts the absolute.
findings.fix: Scope the claim to pipeline-provisioned resources, e.g. 'so no pipeline-provisioned address enters OCI that IPAM doesn't already know about; out-of-band changes are caught by the scheduled reconciliation in Day-2'.

findings.claim: Failover option: 'anycast (advertise a /32 service IP via BGP over the DRG)' / §9 'advertise the DNS service /32 via BGP over the DRG v2, equal routes to both members' for members INSIDE the hub VCN
findings.problem: OCI DRG BGP peering is documented for FastConnect virtual circuits and IPSec tunnels (external CPE), not for compute instances inside a VCN. Whether two in-VCN vNIOS members can advertise an anycast /32 to the DRG via BGP is an Oracle-platform capability question the cited sources do not obviously cover; if not implementable, the primary HA design in §5.d/§9 fails. Repeated at line ~240.
findings.fix: Verify against Oracle DRG v2 documentation; if in-VCN BGP peering is not supported, restate anycast as an on-prem/edge advertisement pattern or make the OCI Network Load Balancer VIP the primary intra-OCI failover mechanism.

findings.claim: vNIOS on OCI went GA with NIOS 8.5.2 (CP-2205 as Grid member); 'no first-class OCI Marketplace vNIOS listing'; 'no deep, event-driven cloud-discovery adapter equivalent to the AWS/Azure/GCP Cloud Network Automation connectors'
findings.problem: Load-bearing vendor facts (GA version, validated appliance model, Marketplace absence, connector absence) that drift over time — a negative claim about a marketplace is especially perishable. Vendor sources are cited (Infoblox blog and docs), but a 3PAO would want a dated verification; the chapter hedges the appliance matrix ('version-specific') but not the Marketplace/connector negatives.
findings.fix: Re-verify against Infoblox docs and the OCI Marketplace at review time and add an 'as of <date>' qualifier to the Marketplace-absence and connector-absence statements, matching the hedge already applied to the appliance matrix.

findings.claim: OCI resolver forwarding endpoint 'consumes 2 private IPs in its subnet — one used, one reserved'; listening endpoint 'consumes 1 private IP'
findings.problem: Precise Oracle-platform resource-consumption numbers that only Oracle documentation can confirm. They are internally consistent with the repo's OCI module (oci-lz-automation/OCI-LZ-Infoblox-DDI-Automation-Guide.md lines 335/352 and terraform/dns.tf comments), so if wrong they are wrong everywhere — a single external verification against the cited Oracle private-DNS doc settles all instances.
findings.fix: Verify the 2-IP/1-IP endpoint consumption figures against the cited Oracle Private DNS resolver documentation; correct here and in oci-lz-automation if they differ.

findings.claim: 'OCI runs Government (US Gov / DoD), National Security, EU Sovereign, and dedicated/air-gapped regions' and that sovereign/air-gapped realms 'typically disallow' the outbound-443 Universal DDI path
findings.problem: The OCI realm/region-type list and the connectivity characterization are Oracle facts with no matching source in the chapter's Sources list (the Oracle links cited cover DNS, landing zones, IAM, and images — not realms). The paragraph is decision-driving (it steers gov customers to vNIOS Grid over Universal DDI).
findings.fix: Add an Oracle source for realm/region types (e.g. the OCI Government Cloud / dedicated-region documentation) to the Sources list, or soften the realm enumeration to 'sovereign and government realms' without naming specific offerings.

findings.claim: Overlapping CIDRs across clouds are the number-one cause of failed transit/peering and un-routable hybrid connectivity
findings.problem: A superlative ranking ("number-one cause") asserted as fact with no source anywhere in the chapter or its Sources list; nothing in the corpus supports the ranking, and a hostile reviewer will ask 'per whom, measured how'.
findings.fix: Soften to an unranked statement (e.g. "a leading and hard-to-remediate cause") or attach a citable source for the ranking.

findings.claim: Anycast "gives instant failover if a member dies"
findings.problem: Anycast failover is bounded by route-withdrawal/health-check convergence (seconds, depending on BGP/OSPF timers), not instant; §6.6 itself tells the reader to test that "anycast reconverges", implicitly conceding a convergence window and mildly contradicting "instant".
findings.fix: Replace "instant failover" with "automatic failover within routing-convergence time" or similar.

findings.claim: The ServiceNow CPG Terraform Connector ingests each platform's terraform/ module as a catalog item mapping form fields to tfvars, and the Service Graph Connector for Infoblox keeps cmdb_ci_ip_network reconciled from Infoblox IPAM
findings.problem: Specific third-party product capabilities (catalog ingestion of arbitrary Terraform modules; CMDB class populated) that cannot be verified from in-repo SSOTs; the ServiceNow Store links in Sources support product existence but the capability details need verification against ServiceNow product documentation before an assessor relies on them.
findings.fix: Verify both capability claims against the ServiceNow Store/product docs (already linked in Sources) and pin the connector versions in Chapter 7 where the full model lives; no truth judgment made here.

findings.claim: Section 7.4 maps the chapter's mechanisms to nine controls: AC-5/AC-6 (approval + SoD), AU-2/AU-6/AU-12 and CM-3/CM-5 (change record + audit trail), CM-6 (validation gates), CM-8 (reclaim-on-delete).
findings.problem: The closure registry (aan-compliance-spine.yml, book-ddi-servicenow entries at ~lines 358-361) registers only THREE closures for this book: CM-3, CM-5, and AU-2. The other six controls (AC-5, AC-6, AU-6, AU-12, CM-6, CM-8) have no registry backing from this book. The spine also attributes the separation-of-duties gate to CM-5 (Access Restrictions for Change), while the chapter leads with AC-5/AC-6 for the same gate — a reviewer will ask which mapping is authoritative. All nine control ids and their implied titles ARE correct against reference/nist-800-53r5-controls.json (AC-5 = Separation of Duties, CM-6 = Configuration Settings, CM-8 = System Component Inventory, etc.), so this is a registry-alignment gap, not a catalog error. Note CM-8 for DDI inventory is registered to book-sn-cmdb and book-ddi-xplat in the spine, not this book.
findings.fix: Either trim the 7.4 mapping to the three spine-registered closures (CM-3, CM-5, AU-2) and label the rest as supporting/informal family touchpoints, or add the missing closure rows to aan-compliance-spine.yml for book-ddi-servicenow so the chapter and the registry agree.

findings.claim: Load-bearing vendor claims: (a) 'this is assembly of certified products' — ServiceNow ships a Terraform connector and Infoblox ships a *certified* Service Graph Connector; (b) the CPG Terraform Connector ingests a Terraform module as a catalog item and runs plan/apply on 'Terraform OSS/Cloud/Enterprise' via a MID Server with a native approval workflow (line 35); (c) the Service Graph Connector imports Infoblox data into the specific CMDB tables cmdb_ci_ip_network and cmdb_ci_ip_network_subnet (line 36); (d) HashiCorp's ServiceNow Catalog for Terraform offers the same speculative-plan-approve-apply pattern for TFC/TFE (lines 41-43); (e) 'FedRAMP-authorized ServiceNow (GovCloud) instance' (line 71); (f) the two ServiceNow Store sys_id URLs in Sources (lines 98-99).
findings.problem: None of these are verifiable against in-repo SSOTs; the chapter's core framing ('assembly of certified products, not custom glue') rests on the certified/Store status of both connectors, and the exact CMDB table names and Terraform-edition support matrix are the kind of specifics a 3PAO would spot-check against current vendor documentation. Not judged true or false. Vendor source links ARE present in the Sources section, satisfying the series' vendor-sourcing convention.
findings.fix: Before publication, re-verify against the live ServiceNow Store listings and Infoblox/HashiCorp docs: the 'certified' designation, the supported Terraform editions for the CPG connector, the exact CMDB CI classes populated by the Infoblox Service Graph Connector, and that the two Store sys_id URLs still resolve.

findings.claim: "the execution and credential path never leaves the ATO boundary"
findings.problem: The absolute "never" in the first boundary bullet is contradicted two bullets later by the acknowledged Universal DDI SaaS exception, where API calls (carrying the resolved credential) cross the ATO boundary to Infoblox's SaaS. A 3PAO would flag the unqualified claim even though the exception is gated.
findings.fix: Qualify the first bullet, e.g. "...never leaves the ATO boundary on the self-managed (NIOS/vNIOS) path; the Universal DDI SaaS path is the explicit, gated exception below."

findings.claim: "Chapters 1–6 build DDI platform-first ... then (in each chapter's §8) put a ServiceNow front door on the result"
findings.problem: True for Chapters 1–5 (ServiceNow subsection sits under each '## 8. IPAM discovery & automation'), but Chapter 6's ServiceNow section is §6.9 ('Governed self-service across the estate'), which this same file cites correctly in its Sources ('Chapter 6 §6.9'). §6.8 is the rollout sequence.
findings.fix: Rephrase to "in each platform chapter's §8 (and Chapter 6's §6.9)" or "in each chapter's ServiceNow section".

findings.claim: Prerequisites cite "a FedRAMP-authorized ServiceNow instance" and "the two certified Store apps (CPG Terraform Connector, Service Graph Connector for Infoblox)"
findings.problem: ServiceNow's FedRAMP authorization status and the ServiceNow Store 'certified' status of both apps are external-vendor facts not verifiable against in-repo SSOTs; the Sources section links the Store listings but certification status can change. Not judged true or false — flagged for external verification per review policy.
findings.fix: Verify current Store certification status and ServiceNow FedRAMP marketplace status at review time; consider adding an 'as of' qualifier or routing these through the vendor-sources convention.

findings.claim: A.1.2 table, Google Cloud row: compute = "`n2`/`c3` class ×N (chapter 3)"
findings.problem: Chapter 3 (03-gcp.md §4 line 73 and §9 line 209) specifies the N1 general-purpose series only — it never mentions n2 or c3. The parenthetical "(chapter 3)" presents this as derived from the chapter, so the appendix directly contradicts its cited source on the machine family that drives GCP sizing/cost.
findings.fix: Change the row to the N1 series to match chapter 3, or (if n2/c3 is the intended guidance) update chapter 3 §4/§9 first and keep the two in lockstep.

findings.claim: A.1.2 table, AWS row: compute = "Compute-optimised/EBS-optimised instance ×N (chapter 2)"
findings.problem: Chapter 2 (02-aws.md §4 line 76 and §9 line 225) specifies M7i / R7i shapes (general-purpose / memory-optimised) for NIOS 9.0.5+. Neither is a compute-optimised (C-family) instance, so the appendix's characterisation contradicts the chapter it cites.
findings.fix: Replace "Compute-optimised/EBS-optimised instance" with "M7i/R7i shapes (NIOS 9.0.5+)" to match chapter 2 §4/§9.

findings.claim: A.1.2 table, AWS storage cell: "gp3/io2 EBS, sized as above"
findings.problem: Chapter 2 says only "EBS root + data volume" / "EBS data volume" and never names gp3 or io2; the volume-type recommendation appears only here with no source, while the row's citation implies it comes from chapter 2.
findings.fix: Either add the gp3/io2 recommendation to chapter 2 §4/§9 (with a source) or hedge the cell (e.g. "EBS data volume — type per the current vNIOS-for-AWS guide").

findings.claim: A.2.4 table: "Route 53 Resolver supports v6" (AWS row) and "Cloud DNS AAAA + inbound/outbound v6" (Google Cloud row, line 86)
findings.problem: These are unhedged cloud-provider capability claims. Unlike the Azure and OCI rows (which say "verify"/"confirm"), these two rows assert support flatly, and the Sources section cites only Infoblox pages — no AWS or Google documentation backs them.

findings.claim: kev_check.py sets `sla_days = 14 if exposed else 28   # BOD 22-01` — i.e., BOD 22-01 mandates a 14-day SLA for internet-facing KEV findings and 28 days otherwise.

A 3PAO would reject an SLA artifact derived this way.
findings.fix: Use the KEV catalog's own `dueDate` per CVE (kev_ids[cve]['dueDate']) as the BOD 22-01 due date; if an exposure-based model is wanted, attribute it to the BOD 26-04 four-variable model (which the spine cites for SI-2(3)) rather than BOD 22-01.

findings.claim: `docker exec ddi-bind dig @127.0.0.1 app.app.example.test A +short   # → 10.20.0.15` — the in-container query demonstrates the internal view.
findings.problem: The internal view matches clients in 10.0.0.0/8 or 172.16.0.0/12. A dig from inside the container to 127.0.0.1 sources from 127.0.0.1, which matches neither, so BIND falls through to the external view (`match-clients { any; }`) and returns NXDOMAIN — identical to the 'external client' line. As written, the lab's core split-horizon success criterion cannot be reproduced; both commands give the same answer.
findings.fix: Add `localhost;` (or 127.0.0.0/8) to the internal view's match-clients, or run the internal query from a second container attached to a 10.x docker network, and keep the external query from the host.

findings.claim: Step 2 is titled 'custom SIT + DLP in simulation mode' and creates a custom EMP-ID rule package, presented as the corroborated custom SIT the DLP policy exercises.
findings.problem: The rule package ($rulePack) is created and never referenced again; the DLP rule that follows keys on the built-in 'U.S. Social Security Number (SSN)' SIT, and the test documents are seeded with fake SSNs. The custom SIT contributes nothing to the exercise or the evidence, so the step's headline claim is not demonstrated by its own commands.
findings.fix: Either have New-DlpComplianceRule reference the custom EMP SIT (and seed EMP-pattern test docs), or drop the rule-package block and retitle the step around the built-in SSN SIT.

findings.claim: Learners should review false positives 'before switching `-Mode` to `Enforce`'.
findings.problem: The documented value set for New-/Set-DlpCompliancePolicy -Mode is Enable / TestWithNotifications / TestWithoutNotifications / Disable; 'Enforce' is not an accepted value, so a learner following the instruction verbatim would hit a parameter error. Microsoft cmdlet parameter — verify against current ExchangeOnlineManagement docs before changing.
findings.fix: Verify the current -Mode enum and, if confirmed, change the instruction to 'switching -Mode to Enable (enforcement)'.

findings.claim: SigninLogs ResultType 500121 captures denied/timed-out MFA prompts for the MFA-fatigue rule, and `az sentinel alert-rule create --scheduled` accepts the shown inline-JSON shape (including incidentConfiguration.createIncident).
findings.problem: Microsoft error-code semantics and the sentinel CLI extension's parameter shape are external product facts the SSOTs cannot confirm; if either has drifted, the seeded detection or the deployment command fails silently for learners.
findings.fix: Re-verify code 500121 and the az sentinel extension schema against current Microsoft docs during the next research pass; no in-repo change if confirmed.

findings.claim: SC-401 (Information Security Administrator) is 'successor to the retired SC-400'.
findings.problem: Exam lineage/retirement status is an external Microsoft fact not covered by any in-repo SSOT; if SC-400 is not actually retired (or the successor framing changes), the row's rationale is wrong.
findings.fix: Confirm SC-400 retirement and SC-401 succession on Microsoft Learn during the weekly link/research pass.

findings.claim: PIM requires Entra ID P2, and PIM audit events are retrievable with `-Filter "loggedByService eq 'PIM'"` via Get-MgAuditLogDirectoryAudit.
findings.problem: Licensing tier and the exact loggedByService string are Microsoft product facts outside the in-repo SSOTs; the evidence-export step (the slot-01 artifact) silently returns nothing if the service name differs.
findings.fix: Verify the loggedByService value ('PIM') against current Graph directoryAudit documentation; no change if confirmed.

findings.claim: verify() implements closure-by-observation: 're-reads the same surface, confirms the drift is gone' (header lines 3-8; README step 5 says it 'proves closure by observation').
findings.problem: Closure is inferred from ABSENCE, and a failed re-read looks like success. If the post-remediation read errors, ComplianceIngest._rest returns a single READ_FAILED sentinel finding whose asset is the REST message name ('graph'/'arm'); verify() only fails when readings[i].asset === task.asset, so the sentinel never matches and verify returns {closed:true} with a RETEST_PASSED stamp. A dead tenant connection therefore closes the task with passing CA-7 evidence — the exact outcome the MID script's own doctrine forbids ('a failed read must never look like a clean posture'). Same fail-open holds for any reason the asset drops out of the response (wrong task.surface — anything not 'azure' silently re-reads M365 — paging, deleted resource, _classify only emitting non-compliant rows).
findings.fix: Make verify fail closed: treat any READ_FAILED sentinel in the readings as retest-inconclusive (escalate, do not close); require an affirmative observation of task.asset in a successful read before stamping RETEST_PASSED; validate task.surface explicitly instead of defaulting to M365.

findings.claim: Header lines 13-15: 'if the identity is detected holding write scopes over the governed estate, the gate refuses to run at all'; rest/README.md lines 17-19: 'ComplianceGate refuses to run if it detects a *.ReadWrite.* grant' — stated as present-tense structural fact ('Least privilege is structural, not aspirational').
findings.problem: _identityHoldsWrite() returns false unconditionally in production; the write-scope refusal only exists under test_mode via the test_fixture_write_scopes property. The ATF test write_scope_voids_attestation passes against the fixture while the production path is a no-op that always reports 'no write scopes' — a safety check that works only in test mode, with the test suite providing false assurance that the invariant is enforced. The app's central attestation argument ('authority to attest depends on its inability to actuate') rests on this stub.
findings.fix: Either implement the Graph appRoleAssignments/oauth2PermissionGrants read and refuse on *.ReadWrite.* over governed surfaces, or make the unimplemented state fail closed (refuse to run until the check is configured). Reword ComplianceGate header and rest/README.md to describe the check as required per-tenant completion, not shipped behavior.

findings.claim: atf/README.md: the suite is 'Runnable via x_ssa_fed_compliance.test_mode = true'; the three Script Includes are presented as importable sys_script_include records in scope x_ssa_fed_compliance.
findings.problem: All three Script Includes call `new GSLog(...)` in initialize() (ComplianceIngest.js:21, ComplianceReconcile.js:16, ComplianceGate.js:22). GSLog is a GLOBAL Script Include; from a scoped application it must be referenced as `new global.GSLog(...)`. As written, initialize() throws 'GSLog is not defined' in the x_ssa_fed_compliance scope, so no class can be instantiated and none of the seven ATF tests in atf/README.md can execute as specified — including in test_mode.
findings.fix: Use `new global.GSLog(...)` (GSLog is scope-accessible but needs the global prefix) or replace with gs.info/gs.warn/gs.error scoped logging.

findings.claim: README step 2 and flow-blueprint.md step 3: an unreconciled asset raises 'a CM-8 inventory finding'; ComplianceIngest.js lines 48-49: on read failure 'the failure itself is raised as an attest.conmon.rollup finding'.
findings.problem: Two contradictions in the synthetic-finding routing. (a) raiseUnreconciled() emits class 'attest.conmon.rollup', which control-map.json binds to CA-7 / slot-04-telemetry / approval 'automated' — there is no CM-8 finding class anywhere in the map (CM-8 closes in Book 01, outside this app's projection), so the advertised 'CM-8 inventory defect' is actually booked as an auto-approved CA-7 change; a 3PAO tracing the CM-8 claim to the task record finds CA-7. (b) The READ_FAILED sentinel finding carries asset 'graph'/'arm', which can never reconcile to a CI, so under the app's own 'no CI, no task' invariant (Flow 1 step 3) it is suppressed and replaced by raiseUnreconciled — the promised read-failure task is never opened as described.
findings.fix: Either add an explicit inventory/read-failure finding class with the intended control binding and exempt synthetic findings from the CI-join, or correct README/flow prose to say the defect is raised under the CA-7 conmon class and state how synthetic findings bypass reconciliation.

findings.claim: Flow 1 step 4: 'Look up the finding class in data/control-map.json → task type, approval, SLA class, KSI, slot'; README step 3: task opened 'with owner, SLA class, and KSI binding from data/control-map.json'.
findings.problem: control-map.json entries contain no SLA-class field and no owner field (fields are title, control, task_type, approval, actuation, ksi, slot, note — confirmed by REQUIRED in validate_day2_control_maps.py). Two documents claim the map supplies data it does not carry; a builder following the blueprint cannot produce the described lookup.
findings.fix: Either add sla_class (and an owner-resolution rule) to each control-map.json entry, or amend flow-blueprint.md and README.md to state where SLA class and owner actually come from.

findings.claim: ComplianceIngest 'pulls M365 (Graph/SCuBA/Purview) and Azure (Resource Graph/Defender/Update Manager) control state' (README table, echoed in ComplianceIngest.js header lines 5-8).
findings.problem: Purview label/DLP posture is read nowhere: not in ComplianceIngest.js (only CA policies + secureScoreControlProfiles), not in mid/compliance-validate.sh (only ScubaGear + az graph), not in rest/README.md. Azure Resource Graph ingestion exists only as a placeholder comment in the MID script; the JS ingestAzure path calls ARM directly. Additionally, ComplianceIngest.js line 33 says the SCuBA MID verdict JSON is ingested 'rather than re-running the scan here', but no mechanism anywhere in the kit moves the verdict file from the MID host into the instance or parses it.
findings.fix: Either add the Purview read and the SCuBA-verdict ingestion path (even as explicit stubs), or narrow the README/header capability list to what the skeleton actually reads.

findings.claim: Azure state is read via GET '/providers/Microsoft.Security/assessments?api-version=2021-06-01' and '/providers/Microsoft.Maintenance/updates?api-version=2023-04-01' against management.azure.com; _classify assumes Graph secureScoreControlProfiles rows carry state 'disabled' / status 'Unhealthy'; rest/README.md asserts the Graph scopes needed are Policy.Read.All, Directory.Read.All, SecurityEvents.Read.All and that GCC Moderate is served by graph.microsoft.com/management.azure.com.
findings.problem: These are Microsoft-API facts the repo SSOTs cannot confirm and the build depends on. Specific concerns to verify against Microsoft docs before sub-prod build: Microsoft.Security/assessments is a scoped resource (normally /subscriptions/{id}/providers/...) — the tenant-root path as written may 404; Microsoft.Maintenance/updates is likewise resource-scoped and Update Manager patch state is normally queried via Resource Graph patchassessmentresources; secureScoreControlProfiles rows do not use 'disabled'/'Unhealthy' values in the fields _classify checks, so that endpoint may never yield a baseline-drift finding; and the exact api-versions and GCC endpoint statements need vendor-source confirmation per the series' vendor-claims rule.
findings.fix: Verify each path, api-version, response shape, and required Graph permission against Microsoft documentation; add 'Vendor sources:' style citations or mark these lines explicitly as per-tenant completion items.

findings.claim: README line 46 / ComplianceIngest header: test_mode 'returns deterministic fixtures... Never enable in production'; evidence stamps feed the Book 04 attestation stream and KSI pipeline (CA-7).
findings.problem: Nothing but a docs sentence prevents x_ssa_fed_compliance.test_mode=true on a production instance, and _stamp() records task, asset, verdict, retested_at, boundary — no test_mode/fixture marker. With the property flipped, ComplianceReconcile reconciles any asset to 'fixture-ci-sysid' and ComplianceGate emits RETEST_PASSED evidence derived from fixtures that is indistinguishable from real CA-7 evidence in the attestation stream. A hostile ISSO will ask how attestation evidence proves it was not produced under test_mode.
findings.fix: Stamp test_mode/fixture provenance into every evidence record (and have Flow 3 refuse to emit fixture-stamped evidence to the attestation stream); optionally hard-refuse test_mode when the instance is production.

findings.claim: Header: 'Exit non-zero on ANY read failure — a failed read must never look like a clean posture.'
findings.problem: The script always exits 0, including when both placeholder verdicts are READ_FAILED. The verdict content is honest (READ_FAILED, not fake compliance), so this is not fail-open, but the stated exit-code contract is unmet and a caller keying on exit status would treat a failed run as success.
findings.fix: Have the script exit non-zero when any verdict status is READ_FAILED, or reword the header to say the contract applies after per-tenant completion.

findings.claim: 'the Graph app registration holds Policy.Read.All, Directory.Read.All, SecurityEvents.Read.All (and the narrow task-creation scope)'.
findings.problem: Task creation is a ServiceNow-side capability of the scoped app, not a Microsoft Graph permission — no Graph scope grants ServiceNow task creation. Listing it inside the Graph app registration's grant set muddies the least-privilege enumeration a reviewer would audit against the actual app registration.
findings.fix: Move the task-creation authority statement out of the Graph-scope list (it belongs to the ServiceNow app scope/ACLs) and keep the Graph list strictly to Graph permissions.

findings.claim: Header (lines 4-7) claims the gate 're-reads the target through Graph and confirms the intended state actually took — closure proven by observation, not by the write returning 200'.
findings.problem: verify() only does GET /users/{userId} and returns ok if the read itself succeeded (any 2xx). It never compares the returned state to the intended state (e.g. accountEnabled=false after a leaver disable), and for group/license/guest actions it reads the wrong object entirely (the user, not the membership/license/invitation). A failed disable passes the verify gate and gets stamped as CM-3/AU-2 evidence — the exact 'write returned 200' failure mode the header says it prevents.
findings.fix: Make verify() action-aware: fetch the relevant object and assert the expected property (accountEnabled, member present, license in assignedLicenses, etc.); return ok=false with the observed-vs-expected delta in evidence when the state does not match.

findings.claim: preflight() enforces 'a privileged grant must carry an expiry (AC-6)' via `request.privileged === true`.
findings.problem: Strict equality to boolean true. The flow blueprint passes `inputs.privileged` straight from catalog variables, which in ServiceNow arrive as strings ('true'). 'true' === true is false, so the AC-6 expiry gate silently never fires and a standing privileged grant passes preflight — an error state that looks like success, and it defeats the atf negative-standing-privilege test's purpose in real (non-canned) input shapes.
findings.fix: Coerce: `var priv = request.privileged === true || request.privileged === 'true';` (same normalization for expiry emptiness), and add an ATF case that passes the string form.

findings.claim: Step 4 actuates with `var r = c[inputs.action](inputs.target_id, inputs.opts); // dispatch by action`.
findings.problem: Unvalidated dynamic dispatch on a flow input. There is no allowlist, so `inputs.action = '_graph'` invokes the internal method with attacker-chosen HTTP verb (target_id) and path (opts) — an arbitrary Microsoft Graph call under the app's credential alias, bypassing every per-action mapping in the control map. `initialize`/`type` are also reachable. This is a privilege-escalation surface inside the very component whose stated purpose is scoped, individually-approved writes.
findings.fix: Dispatch through an explicit allowlist keyed by the catalog item's control_key (e.g. a map of action name -> function), rejecting anything not in the map; never index the client object with raw input.

findings.claim: One generic call `c[inputs.action](inputs.target_id, inputs.opts)` drives all seven client methods.
findings.problem: Signature mismatch: createUser expects a payload object (uses payload.upn), addGroupMember expects (groupId, userId), inviteGuest expects (email, redirectUrl), resetMfaMethod expects (userId, methodId). The uniform (target_id, opts) shape cannot correctly invoke at least createUser and inviteGuest as written — the joiner and guest-invite happy paths are broken as specified, so the blueprint cannot be rebuilt 'exactly' as it claims.
findings.fix: Document per-action argument mapping in the dispatch table (see the allowlist fix above), or normalize all client methods to a single (request) object signature.

findings.claim: disableUser: 'Revoke refresh tokens / active sessions so the disable takes effect now'; map note and leaver-completion flow claim evidenced 'disable + revoke sessions'.
findings.problem: The revokeSignInSessions result is discarded — the method returns the PATCH result only. If the revoke call fails (its _graph returns ok:false, unchecked), the leaver still closes with success evidence while sessions remain live, and the leaver-completion flow's 'sessions revoked' evidence claim is false. A revoke failure is indistinguishable from success.
findings.fix: Capture the revoke result and fold it into the return value (`ok: r.ok && revoke.ok`, plus per-step status), so the verify gate and leaver-completion flow can see a partial de-provision.

findings.claim: preflight() enforces CM-5 separation of duties (requester != approver).
findings.problem: The check is guarded by `if (request.requester_id && ...)` — an empty/undefined requester_id skips the SoD comparison entirely and preflight returns ok. A request with an unpopulated requester field (or both fields empty) bypasses the CM-5 gate rather than failing closed.
findings.fix: Fail closed: if requester_id or approver_id is missing, return {ok:false, reason:'SoD indeterminate: requester/approver not populated'}.

findings.claim: saas.approve note: 'Any integration receiving privileged scopes, or any SCIM path, requires a security approver distinct from the business owner. Enforced pre-flight by EntraHelpdeskGate, not by convention.' (Also asserted in the spine's book-sn-saas AC-5 row.)
findings.problem: EntraHelpdeskGate.preflight implements only two checks: requester != approver, and privileged-implies-expiry. It has no SCIM-path awareness, no scope inspection, and no 'security approver distinct from the business owner' logic. The claimed mechanism does not exist in the shipped code — exactly the 'closes with no mechanism' pattern a 3PAO probes.
findings.fix: Either extend the gate (scim_path/privileged_scopes inputs, approver-role check) or soften the note to say the FLOW's approval routing enforces it and the gate enforces SoD + expiry only.

findings.claim: _comment: onboarding a SaaS 'is the moment ~18 controls are closed at the workflow plane'.
findings.problem: The map itself binds 24 catalog items to 24 distinct controls, and the spine carries exactly 24 book-sn-saas closures. '~18' cannot be reproduced from any current SSOT — it looks like a stale count from before the map grew.
findings.fix: Change to '24 controls' (or 'two dozen'), or derive the number in the render pipeline so it cannot drift again.

findings.claim: Update set contains 'Catalog items + variable sets — one per catalog entry across the four control maps (helpdesk-, landingzone-, appreg-, telephony-control-map.json)'.
findings.problem: The directory holds FIVE control maps — saas-control-map.json (24 items, Lane F) is omitted here and from the top-level README's 'What's here' table, yet it declares itself part of this app's governed catalog (its items cite EntraHelpdeskGate enforcement and graph-via-mid/acme-via-mid actuation) and is CI-validated with the other four. A reviewer cannot tell whether the SaaS lane's 24 catalog items ship in the update set or not.
findings.fix: Either add saas-control-map.json to both READMEs and the update-set contents (five maps, 55 items per the validator), or state explicitly that Lane F belongs to Vol VII Book 06 and ships separately.

findings.claim: 'Never enable test_mode in production' (comment only, repeated in atf/README.md).
findings.problem: test_mode is gated solely by a system property readable/settable like any other; there is no code-level production guard. If set in production, the Client returns canned successes without actuating and the Gate returns verified:true — the flow would mint false CM-3/AU-2 evidence records end-to-end (request 'closed with evidence' for actions that never happened). For an evidence-generating app, a comment is not a control.
findings.fix: Add an instance guard (e.g. refuse test_mode unless the instance name matches a sub-prod pattern / a second property only present in sub-prod), and stamp `test_mode: true` into every evidence object so fabricated evidence is self-identifying.

findings.claim: All 10 helpdesk items declare actuation 'graph-via-mid'; entra.credential.account_unlock and entra.access.ca_exception included.
findings.problem: The shipped client implements 7 methods (createUser, disableUser, resetPassword, resetMfaMethod, addGroupMember, assignLicense, inviteGuest) — there is no unlock or Conditional-Access method, so two items have a declared Graph actuation path with no actuator. Additionally, Entra ID exposes no Graph 'account unlock' operation (smart lockout is not admin-clearable via Graph) — whether unlock is implementable as specified needs external verification against Microsoft Graph documentation.
findings.fix: Implement/document the actuator per item (unlock may reduce to password reset or an Entra-side wait; CA exception should reference the Vol VII Book 02 actuation record), or change the actuation value for items the client does not serve.

findings.claim: resetMfaMethod issues DELETE /users/{id}/authentication/methods/{methodId}.
findings.problem: Microsoft Graph deletes authentication methods per typed collection (…/authentication/phoneMethods/{id}, fido2Methods/{id}, microsoftAuthenticatorMethods/{id}, etc.); the generic authentication/methods collection is documented as list/get, not delete. As written the call likely 404s/405s for every MFA reset. External verification against current Graph docs required — do not judge true/false from here.
findings.fix: Verify against Graph v1.0 docs; if confirmed, pass the method type and build the typed path.

findings.claim: The app registration 'holds LEAST-PRIVILEGE, individually consented Graph scopes (e.g. User.ReadWrite.All, Group.ReadWrite.All, UserAuthenticationMethod.ReadWrite.All) — never Directory-wide admin.'
findings.problem: Two issues. (1) Misleading framing: User.ReadWrite.All and Group.ReadWrite.All ARE tenant-wide write permissions over every user/group; contrasting them with 'Directory-wide admin' overstates the least-privilege posture — an ISSO will read 'least privilege' against the actual scope grant. (2) Sufficiency/accuracy of the example scopes for the implemented operations (passwordProfile PATCH under application permissions, /invitations, assignLicense) needs external verification against Graph permission reference — e.g. password writes may require User-PasswordProfile.ReadWrite.All and cannot target privileged users.
findings.fix: Replace the example list with the per-operation least-privileged application permissions from the Graph permissions reference (with a 'Vendor sources:' link per the series spec), and drop the 'never Directory-wide admin' contrast or qualify it.

findings.claim: resetPassword sends opts.tempPassword in the PATCH body; the update-set README claims 'no secrets in the record'.
findings.problem: The temporary password is a plaintext secret traveling through catalog variables and Flow inputs (flow-blueprint step 4 passes inputs.opts), which are persisted in Flow execution contexts and visible to anyone with flow-operations access; nothing specifies how tempPassword is generated or that it is excluded from logging/evidence. The 'no secrets in code' claim covers the credential alias but not this data path.
findings.fix: Generate the temp password server-side inside the client (never as a flow input), mark any password variable as masked/password type, and explicitly exclude it from outputs.result and evidence objects.

findings.claim: Negative test: 'An action whose target does not match an authoritative identity routes to the reconcile-exception queue (CM-8), not to closure'; top README says every request is a 'typed catalog item against the reconciled identity CI'.
findings.problem: In the flow's canonical order, reconciliation is step 6 — AFTER actuation (step 4). Nothing in preflight (step 2) checks that the target matches an authoritative identity, so the Graph write executes against the unreconciled target and only the paperwork is quarantined afterward. The CM-8 'gate' as specified prevents closure, not actuation — weaker than what both READMEs imply.
findings.fix: Add a target-reconciliation check to preflight (target CI resolves to an authoritative IPAM/DDI-keyed identity, else refuse before approval), and reword the ATF row to state what is actually asserted.

findings.claim: 'Under GCC Moderate the Graph host resolves to the commercial endpoint that serves that boundary: graph.microsoft.com.'
findings.problem: Vendor-endpoint claim about Microsoft service topology; consistent with the series' GCC-Moderate doctrine but it is exactly the kind of vendor claim the AAN authoring spec requires a 'Vendor sources:' citation for, and none is given in this kit. Not judged true/false here.
findings.fix: Add the Microsoft Graph national-cloud-deployments doc reference alongside the claim.

findings.claim: Remaining step 4: 'Wire the control-map CI check (regen-and-diff vs aan-compliance-spine.yml) into the book CI' — listed as not done.
findings.problem: The check is already wired: validate_day2_control_maps.py runs in .pre-commit-config.yaml (line ~212, path-filtered to servicenow-day2/) and in .github/workflows/aan-authorities-drift.yml (line 115), and the same README's table calls the helpdesk map 'CI-checked'. The remaining-steps list contradicts both.
findings.fix: Strike step 4 as done (matching the strikethrough style of steps 1-2), or narrow it to whatever residual 'book CI' wiring is genuinely outstanding.

findings.claim: Table row: appreg-control-map.json = 'Lane E app-registration lifecycle bindings (IA-5(2)/SC-17/AC-6)'.
findings.problem: The map also binds AC-2 (appreg.request, machine-JML) — the control the spine's book-day2-appreg lane leads with. The README's control list under-reports its own map.
findings.fix: List all four: AC-2/IA-5(2)/SC-17/AC-6.

findings.claim: Volume map table 'Six books, two moves' listing VII-00 through VII-05
findings.problem: The spine registers SEVEN Vol VII books: book-sn-saas (Vol_VII_Book_06 SaaS Integration Governance) exists in aan-compliance-spine.yml but is absent from the deck's volume map, its callout ('Reconcile once... ship it as an app (05)'), and the notes. The overview deck contradicts the book registry SSOT.
findings.fix: Add a VII-06 row (SaaS Integration Governance, SA-9) and change 'Six books' to 'Seven books', updating callout/notes accordingly.

findings.claim: RA-5 titled 'Vulnerability Monitoring' in the Authorities Closed Here table
findings.problem: Official r5.2 title (and the spine's own closure row for book-sn-azure) is 'Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning'. The notes claim the table 'mirrors the spine's generated rows', so the truncated title is a mirror that doesn't match its source.
findings.fix: Use the full title 'Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning'.

findings.claim: SC-17 titled 'PKI Certificates' in the Authorities Closed Here table
findings.problem: Official catalog and spine title is 'Public Key Infrastructure Certificates'. Notes claim the slide mirrors the generated spine rows; the abbreviated title does not match the SSOT.
findings.fix: Use 'Public Key Infrastructure Certificates'.

findings.claim: 'Mirror the generated rows' — table lists IA-5(2), SC-17, AC-6
findings.problem: Spine closures for book-day2-appreg are AC-2, IA-5(2), SC-17, AC-6 (four rows). The deck omits AC-2 (Account Management — the machine-JML lifecycle the deck itself argues for) while claiming to mirror the generated rows.
findings.fix: Add the AC-2 row or drop the 'mirror the generated rows' claim in notes.

findings.claim: 'Mirror the book's generated Authorities-Closed-Here rows' — table lists AC-2, IA-5, AC-6
findings.problem: Spine closures for book-day2-helpdesk are AC-2, IA-5, AC-6, AC-3 (Access Enforcement). The deck omits AC-3 while its notes assert it mirrors the generated rows.
findings.fix: Add the AC-3 row or reword the notes to say 'selected closures'.

findings.claim: Table title 'Five books across the day-2 surface' over four rows (IX-01..IX-04)
findings.problem: The count of five is only reproducible if the reader silently includes Book 00 (this overview) — the table shows four books and the callout says 'four surfaces'. A reviewer will query 5-vs-4.
findings.fix: Retitle 'Four books, four surfaces' or add an IX-00 overview row.

findings.claim: 'A short-lived certificate (ACME)' as the credential mechanism for Entra app registrations
findings.problem: Entra app-registration certificate credentials are not natively issued via ACME; the cited source (ms_appreg quickstart) does not cover ACME issuance for service principals. Whether an ACME-issued short-lived cert workflow applies here needs external verification — not judging it false, but the citation does not support it.
findings.fix: Either cite the actual issuance mechanism/source or soften to 'a short-lived certificate (e.g., from an automated issuance pipeline)'.

findings.claim: 'the CPG Terraform Connector runs a speculative plan the approver reviews before any state changes'
findings.problem: Specific ServiceNow Cloud Provisioning and Governance Terraform Connector capability claim; vendor_sources ['tf_cpg'] is present on the slide, but the speculative-plan-before-approval behavior is a product capability an assessor would verify against ServiceNow docs.
findings.fix: Confirm the tf_cpg doc page states speculative-plan review in the approval step; if not, cite the specific Terraform Connector doc page.

findings.claim: "145 distinct controls span all six content volumes"; per-volume table stops at Vol VI; "258 control-to-book mappings collapse to 145"; subtitle says "seven-volume series"
findings.problem: The source crosswalk (Vol_0_Book_02_FedAAN_Control_Crosswalk.qmd, Date Code 2026-07-14 10:17 ET) now states 146 distinct controls across Volumes I-IX of a ten-volume series, with added rows Vol VII=9, Vol VIII=6, Vol IX=10 and an explicit note that the total moved from 145 to 146 (CM-5 added). The 258 figure appears nowhere in the current source and cannot be reproduced.

findings.claim: Authorities table maps CM-8, CM-2, CM-6 to "KSI-CM" while the notes say the table is "generated from the series compliance spine, not hand-maintained"

findings.claim: 'Assembling eighteen books' / 'the preceding eighteen books' / 'eighteen evidence books (DOCX)' (subtitle, slides 1-3, 13); Book 05 similarly says 'eighteen-book series'.

findings.claim: Slide 4 presents the 95% completion threshold and four-dimension model as 'the KSI-CED-RAT specification distilled' with 'PASS requires completion at or above 95% per dimension'.
findings.problem: The 95% pass line is the UIAO substrate's internal evaluation threshold (as slide 4's own notes eventually concede: 'the pass line the UIAO substrate queries'), but the callout and framing attribute it to the FedRAMP 20x KSI itself. findings.fix: Reword the callout/notes to attribute the 95% threshold to the UIAO evaluation policy ('the substrate's pass line'), not to KSI-CED-RAT's specification.

findings.claim: SA-16 is closed by training the agency's own developers ('Secure delivery... AT-3(3), SA-16', slides 3, 4, 8, 14).
findings.problem: SA-16's official Rev 5 title is 'Developer-provided Training' — it requires the SYSTEM DEVELOPER to provide training on the delivered system to organizational personnel, not the organization to train its developers. Using it as the anchor for an internal secure-coding curriculum inverts the control's subject; an assessor would reject the mapping.
findings.fix: Drop SA-16 from the secure-delivery dimension (AT-3(3) already anchors it) or re-justify it only where an external system developer actually delivers training.

findings.claim: Slide 4: 'zero open risks, zero POA&M items' in the July 4 2026 run; slide 10 step 4: policy MS.AAD.3.1v1 'shows result fail, disposition governed_exception... under a named POA&M ticket'.

findings.fix: Mark the MS.AAD.3.1v1 entry explicitly as an illustrative example, or reconcile the zero-POA&M claim with the governed-exception ledger (e.g., 'zero unmitigated items; governed exceptions tracked as POA&M-linked entries').

findings.claim: 'the 20x KSI-evidence model replaces the 325-control audit binder' (slides 2 and 12).

findings.claim: 'InfoBlox DDI holds a FedRAMP Moderate authorization (CSO FR2017257053)' (slide 3 notes).
findings.problem: Specific CSO ID and authorization level are external Marketplace facts. The slide correctly carries the Marketplace vendor source and a verify-at-procurement caveat, so this is flagged only for the verification queue, not judged true/false.
